## Appendix D Factorization modules over commutative algebras

Let ${\mathcal{Y}}$ be a prestack affine over $X_{\mathrm{dR}}\times T$ , i.e. ${\mathcal{Y}}=\Spec_{X_{\mathrm{dR}}\times T}(A)$ , where

$$ A\in\CommAlg(\D(X)\otimes\QCoh(T)). $$

The goal of this section is to give a rather elementary proof of the following folklore statement.

#### Theorem D.1.

Assume that $A\in\D_{{\operatorname{ind-hol}}}(X)\otimes\QCoh(T)$ . Then we have an equivalence

$$ \QCoh(\hormerxJetsF_{\nabla,T\times U_{\mathrm{dR}}}^{\mer,x}({\mathcal{Y}})_{x})\cong A\operatorname{-FactMod}^{T}. $$

#### Remark D.1.1.

Since the first draft of this paper was circulated, the proof of this statement appeared in [ABC+24] in a greater generality (without the ind-holonomicity condition). However, we still keep this section since the present proof is less technically heavy.

#### Definition D.1.2.

Define lax prestack $\D_{\operatorname{indhol}}$ to be the left Kan extension of the functor

$$ \D_{\operatorname{indhol}}:\AffSch_{\operatorname{ft}}^{\op}\rightarrow\operatorname{Cat}_{\infty} $$

along the embedding $\AffSch_{\operatorname{ft}}^{\op}\hookrightarrow\AffSch^{\op}$ .

For any lax prestack ${\mathcal{Y}}$ define the category of ind-holonomic $D$ -modules on ${\mathcal{Y}}$ as $\Maps({\mathcal{Y}},\D_{\operatorname{indhol}})$ .

#### Remark D.1.3.

Note that for an affine scheme $S$ we get

$$ \D_{\operatorname{indhol}}(S)\cong\underset{S_{i}\in\AffSch_{\operatorname{ft}}S\rightarrow S_{i}}{\text{colim}}\D_{\operatorname{indhol}}(S_{i}). $$

Hence for an affine scheme of finite type we recover the usual definition of ind-holonomic $D$ -modules.

#### Remark D.1.4.

Recall from [Gai19, 2.3.1] that for ${\mathcal{Y}}_{1},{\mathcal{Y}}_{2}\in\laxPreSt$ and $f:{\mathcal{Y}}_{1}\rightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}_{2}$ the map

$$ f^{!}:\D_{\operatorname{indhol}}({\mathcal{Y}}_{2})\rightarrow\D_{\operatorname{indhol}}({\mathcal{Y}}_{1}) $$

admits a left adjoint $f_{!}$ . Hence for a map of curves

$$ X\rightarrow Y $$

and the induces map

$$ f:{\operatorname{Ran}}\rightarrow{\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y} $$

the left adjoint $f_{!}$ to the functor $f^{!}:\D({\operatorname{Ran}})\rightarrow\D({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y})$ is defined on the subcategory $\D_{\operatorname{indhol}}({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y})\subset\D({\operatorname{Ran}}_{Y})$ .

#### Lemma D.1.5.

The object

$$ A\in\D({\operatorname{Ran}})\otimes\QCoh(T) $$

lies in the full subcategory $\D_{{\operatorname{ind-hol}}}({\operatorname{Ran}})\otimes\QCoh(T)$ , therefore the functor ${j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(T)}$ is defined on $A$ .

#### Proof.

It suffices to show that restriction of $A$ to every $X^{K}$ lies in $\D_{{\operatorname{ind-hol}}}(X^{K})\otimes\QCoh(T)$ . Restriction to $X$ lies in $\D_{{\operatorname{ind-hol}}}(X)\otimes\QCoh(T)$ by assumption.

For general $K$ denote by $S_{K}$ the $(1,1)$ -category indexing data $K\twoheadrightarrow I\twoheadrightarrow J$ , where we allow morphisms of diagrams that are contravariant in $I$ and covariant in $J$ , and surjective term-wise. Then one has

$$ (A)_{X^{K}}\cong\underset{K\twoheadrightarrow I\twoheadrightarrow J\in S_{K}}{\text{colim}}({\Delta_{q\circ p}}_{!}\boxtimes\Id_{T})\circ(\Delta_{q}^{!}\boxtimes\Id_{T})(A^{\boxtimes_{T}I}). $$

In particular, since ${j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(T)}$ commutes with colimits and all three operations preserve ind-holonomicity on the first factor we get the result.

∎

Writing any ${\mathcal{F}}\in\QCoh(T)$ as a colimit of ${\mathcal{O}}_{T}$ we see that ${j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(T)}$ is defined on

$$ A\boxtimes_{T}{\mathcal{F}} $$

and

$$ (i_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{T})({j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{T})(A\boxtimes_{T}{\mathcal{F}})\cong(i_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{T})({j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{T})(A)\otimes{\mathcal{F}}. $$

Note that $i_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{\QCoh(T)}$ is continuous and conservative, hence by Barr-Beck Theorem and Proposition C.3.7 we get that

$$ A\operatorname{-FactMod}^{T}\cong(i_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{T})({j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{T})(A)\Mmod(\QCoh(T)). $$

We now calculate $M:=(i_{{\operatorname{Ran}}_{X,x}}^{!}\otimes\Id_{T})({j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}}_{!}\otimes\Id_{T})(A)$ .

#### D.1.6.

We begin by noticing that the functor $j_{{\operatorname{Ran}}}^{!}\times\Id_{\QCoh(T)}$ induces a functor

Consider the following generalization of [GL19, Proposition 5.6.10]:

#### Lemma D.1.8.

let $C$ and $D$ be presentable symmetric monoidal $\infty$ -categories with unit objects $\mathbf{1}_{C}$ and $\mathbf{1}_{D}$ . Assume that tensor product on $C$ and $D$ preserves colimits separately in each variable. Let

$$ G:D\rightarrow C $$

be a lax symmetric monoidal functor.

Assume that partially defined left adjoint $F$ is defined on the full subcategory of $C$ generated by $\mathbf{1}_{C}$ and powers of $\oblv(c)$ for some $c\in\CommAlg(C)$ and $\oblv:\CommAlg(C)\rightarrow C$ . Assume in addition that $F$ is symmetric monoidal and that the unit map $\mathbf{1}_{C}\rightarrow G(\mathbf{1}_{D})$ induces an equivalence $F(\mathbf{1}_{C})\rightarrow\mathbf{1}_{D}$ .

Then the left adjoint $F_{+}$ to the functor

$$ G:\CommAlg(D)\rightarrow\CommAlg(C) $$

induced by $G$ is defined on $c$ and

$$ \oblv(F_{+}(c))\cong F(\oblv(c)). $$

#### Proof.

Denote by $C^{\prime}$ the full subcategory of $C$ generated by $\mathbf{1}_{C}$ and powers of $\oblv(c)$ and by $\iota$ the embedding. By [GL19, Proposition 5.6.6] and [GL19, Proposition 5.6.10] the pair of adjoint functors

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota^{R}} $$

induces the pair of adjoint functors between unital commutative algebra objects

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\CommAlg(C^{\prime})} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\CommAlg(C).} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota_{+}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota^{R}_{+}} $$

Moreover, the pair of adjoint functors

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C^{\prime}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\circ\iota} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota^{R}\circ G} $$

induces the pair of adjoint functors between unital commutative algebra objects

# The canonical global quantization of symplectic varieties in characteristic $p$

**Authors:** Ekaterina Bogdanova Address: Harvard University, USA Email address: ebogdanova@math.harvard.edu , Dmitry Kubrak Address: Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques, France Email address: dmkubrak@gmail.com , Roman Travkin Address: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, Russia Email address: roman.travkin2012@gmail.com and Vadim Vologodsky Address: National Research University “Higher School of Economics”, Russia Email address: vologod@gmail.com

## Abstract

Let $X$ be a smooth symplectic variety over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$ equipped with a restricted structure, which is a class $[\eta]\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X}/d\mathcal{O}_{X})$ whose de Rham differential equals the symplectic form. In this paper we construct a functorial in $(X,[\eta])$ formal quantization of the category $\mathrm{QCoh}(X)$ of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ . We also construct its natural extension to a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories $\mathrm{QCoh}_{h}$ on the product $X^{(1)}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ of the Frobenius twist of $X$ and the projective line ${\mathbb{S}}=\mathbb{P}^{1}$ , viewed as the one-point compactification of $\mathrm{Spec}\ \!k[h]$ . Its global sections over $X^{(1)}\times\{0\}$ is the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ . If $X$ is affine, $\mathrm{QCoh}_{h}$ , restricted to $X^{(1)}\times\mathrm{Spf}\ \!k[[h]]$ , is equivalent to the category of modules over the distinguished “Frobenius-constant” quantization of $(X,[\eta])$ defined in [BK].

## 1. Introduction

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>2$ . In [BK], Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin initiated the study of quantizations of symplectic varieties over $k$ . More precisely, they introduced new notion of a restricted symplectic $k$ -scheme: namely, they consider pairs $(X,[\eta])$ , where $[\eta]$ is a global section of the sheaf $\coker(\mathcal{O}_{X}\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^{1}_{X})$ , such that $\omega:=d([\eta])\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{2}_{X})$ is a symplectic form11 1 One can think of $[\eta]$ as an algebraic analogue of a “contact form” on $X$ .. In the case $H^{i}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X})=0$ for $i=1,2,3$ , they construct the a distinguished “Frobenius-constant” quantization of $(X,[\eta])$ . Roughly speaking, such a quantization is a sheaf $O_{h}$ of associative $k[[h]]$ -algebras on $X$ equipped with two isomorphisms

- • $\mathcal{O}_{X}\xrightarrow{\sim}O_{h}/h$ ,

- • $\mathcal{O}_{X^{(1)}}[[h]]\xrightarrow{\sim}Z(O_{h})$ ,

that are also compatible with the restricted structure given by $[\eta]$ in a certain way. Here $X^{(1)}$ denotes the Frobenius-twist of $X$ and $Z(O_{h})$ is the center of $O_{h}$ . The prototypical example of such a quantization is given by the following: namely, the $k[[h]]$ -version of the Rees algebra $\mathcal{D}_{Y,h}$ of differential operators on $Y$ gives the distinguished Frobenius-constant quantization of $X=T^{*}Y$ with the restricted structure given by the canonical 1-form $\eta$ . An unfortunate feature of the construction is that it is not functorial: there is no natural way to make the distinguished quantization equivariant with respect to automorphisms of $(X,[\eta])$ , and moreover the quantization exists only if we require the aforementioned cohomology vanishing for $X$ . A solution proposed by Kontsevich ([K]) and studied further in ([VdB], [Y]) in characteristic $0$ context is to replace the algebra $O_{h}$ by the corresponding category of modules $O_{h}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . We develop a parallel picture in characteristic $p$ : namely, we show that the category $O_{h}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is functorial in the pair $(X,[\eta])$ and glues to a canonical quantization of the category $\QCoh(X)$ of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ for any restricted symplectic $k$ -scheme $(X,[\eta])$ .

Moreover, our construction allows to extend the range of the quantum parameter $h$ from being a formal variable to a genuine coordinate on ${\mathbb{P}}^{1}$ , where the corresponding category $\QCoh_{h}$ carries a formal resemblance with the twistor space construction appearing in Simpson’s correspondence (see Remark 1.1 below).

### 1.1. Plan of the paper

The idea of “formal geometry” in the sense of Gelfand-Kazhdan is to first deal with differential-geometric questions in the basic case of a formal disc, and then descend to smooth varieties via the corresponding torsor of formal coordinates. As observed by Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin in [BK] in characteristic $p$ one can replace formal disc by the corresponding Frobenius neighborhood of zero, which makes things simpler. To be more precise, the key idea is to consider a smooth $S$ -scheme $X$ of dimension $d$ as a scheme over its Frobenius twist $X^{(1)}$ via the relative Frobenius $F_{X/S}\colon X\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ . This is not only a finite locally free map, but in fact a locally trivial bundle in flat topology: namely, Zariski-locally on $X$ , the fiber product $X\times_{X^{(1)}}X$ splits as $X\times\Spec A_{0}$ where $\Spec A_{0}$ is the Frobenius-neighborhood of 0 in $d$ -dimensional affine space22 2 Explicitly, $A_{0}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{1},\ldots,x_{d}]/x_{1}^{p}=\ldots=x_{d}^{p}=0$ .. One then can consider the canonical torsor $\mathcal{M}_{X}\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ of “Frobenius frames”: a $T$ -point $T\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{X}$ is given by an isomorphism $T\times_{X^{(1)}}X\simeq T\times\Spec A_{0}$ , or, in other words, an identification of (pull-back of) $X$ with the Frobenius neiborhood of zero in an affine space of dimension $d$ over $T$ . The scheme $\mathcal{M}_{X}\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ is a torsor over the group scheme $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ of automorphisms of $\Spec A_{0}$ and many basic objects of differential-geometric nature such as33 3 Strictly speaking one needs to consider their pushforwards to $X^{(1)}$ under relative Frobenius. differential operators $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ , differential 1-forms $\Omega^{1}_{X}$ , vector fields $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ , or just the structure sheaf $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ all come via descent from some representations of $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ . This also gives a way to define differentiable structures on smooth varieties in characteristic $p$ by considering the subgroup $H$ of $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ that stabilizes that “structure” in the case of $X=\Spec A_{0}$ . Prescribing such a structure on a given scheme $X$ then corresponds to a reduction of the $\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ -torsor $\mathcal{M}_{X}\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ to $H$ . We will discuss in some detail how this picture looks in the case of restricted symplectic structure (see Section 2.10).

The above picture motivates considering things like differential operators or symplectic structures in the case of schemes like $\Spec A_{0}$ , or $X$ considered as an $X^{(1)}$ -scheme. These schemes are not smooth, but nevertheless they are pseudo-smooth: namely the sheaf $\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ of relative Kähler differentials is locally free. In Section 2 we develop44 4 In fact, in [BK] Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin freely assume the relevant parts of the theory in the pseudo-smooth (or, in their terminology, quasi-regular) setup, mostly without a proper justification which sometimes leads them to small inaccuracies or even false claims. So we tried to carefully setup the theory, mostly from scratch, only sometimes referencing their results. some basic theory of pseudo-smooth schemes. In fact pseudo-smoothness turns out to be enough to extend most of the standard features of differential geometry of smooth schemes in characteristic $p$ : e.g. the algebra of differential operators is still an Azumaya algebra over the Frobenius twist of the total space of cotangent bundle (Corollary 2.38); there are also versions of Cartier isomorphism (Proposition 2.40) and Milne’s exact sequence (Proposition 2.46). The only difference with the smooth setting is that the notion of Frobenius twist should be slightly modified: namely, instead of Frobenius twist $X^{(1)}\coloneqq X\times_{S,F_{S}}S$ one should consider the schematic image $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow X^{(1)}$ of the relative Frobenius $F_{X/S}\colon X\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ (see Section 2.1 for more details). The corresponding map $F_{X/S}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ induced by $F_{X/S}$ turns out to be finite locally free, and is again a locally trivial bundle with fiber given by the Frobenius neighborhood of 0 in the affine space (Lemma 2.67), however its dimension is now given by $\rk\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ and not the relative dimension of $X$ over $S$ .

The key geometric input which allows to get a good control on pseudo-smooth schemes is their local structure (Proposition 2.35) namely, Zariski locally any pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme $X$ is given by the Frobenius-neighborhood of a closed subscheme in a smooth scheme. This observation allows us to extend most of the results from the smooth to pseudo-smooth setting almost for free.

Moreover, in Section 2.8 we recall the definition of restricted Poisson structure by introducing a restricted Poisson algebra monad. This section is an attempt to explain and motivate the definition of restricted Poisson structure given in [BK]. In Section 2.9 we then discuss restricted symplectic schemes (see Definition 2.60), where a restricted structure exteding a symplectic form $\omega$ has an equivalent description in terms of a class $[\eta]\in\coker(\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X})$ such that $d[\eta]=\omega$ (see Remark 2.61). Finally, in Section 2.10 we endow $\Spec A_{0}$ with a restricted symplectic structure and define the group $G_{0}\subset\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ of its restricted Poisson automorphisms, that plays a very important role in most of the constructions below.

Construction of $\QCoh_{h}$ . Our goal in this paper will be to construct a certain sheaf of categories $\QCoh_{h}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{P}^{1}$ , given a restricted symplectic scheme $(X,[\eta])$ . We want this construction to be functorial in $(X,[\eta])$ and agree55 5 Meaning that the restriction of $\QCoh_{h}$ to the formal neighborhood of 0 in $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ should be given by $O_{h}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . with the distinguished quantization of Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin in the cases when the latter exists. We will discuss other expected properties of $\QCoh_{h}$ slightly later, in Section 1.2 below.

For the reader’s convenience let us note right away that in Section 4 we remind the notion of a quasi-coherent sheaf of (abelian) categories on a scheme or, more generally, an algebraic stack. We then also discuss actions of group schemes on the sheaves of categories in Section 4.2.

Let $\mathbb{S}\coloneqq\mathbb{P}^{1}$ , the idea behind the notation being that $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ resembles a 2-dimensional sphere. In the case $X=T^{*}Y$ with the canonical 1-form $\eta$ one could expect $\QCoh_{h}$ to come as the category of modules over the sheaf of twistor differential operators $\mathcal{D}_{Y,\mathbb{S}}$ . The latter comes as an instance of a $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ -version of the Rees construction (see Section 3.1): namely, $\mathcal{D}_{Y,\mathbb{S}}$ corresponds to differential operators $\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ endowed with the pair of Hodge and conjugate filtrations66 6 That are dual to Hodge and conjugate filtrations on the de Rham complex in a certain sense., see Section 3.2 for more details. Below, we will define $\QCoh_{h}$ by certain universal property, and then check that it is indeed given by $\mathcal{D}_{Y,\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ in the case of $T^{*}Y$ .

The starting point of our construction is the following. Namely, to a restricted symplectic scheme $(X,[\eta])$ one canonically associates a $G_{0}$ -torsor $\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}\rightarrow X^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ of its “Darboux frames”: a $T$ -point $T\rightarrow\mathcal{M}_{X}$ is given by a restricted Poisson isomorphism

$$ T\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}X\simeq T\times\Spec A_{0} $$

(see Construction 2.68). This way a pair $(X,[\eta])$ produces a natural map

$$ \pi\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow BG_{0}. $$

A natural way to define $\QCoh_{h}$ would be to take the pull-back of a certain universal sheaf of categories over $BG_{0}\times\mathbb{S}\simeq[\mathbb{S}/G_{0}]$ via the map $\pi\times\Id\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{S}\rightarrow BG_{0}\times\mathbb{S}$ . This is exactly what we do.

We construct the universal sheaf of categories on $[\mathbb{S}/G_{0}]$ via descent. Namely, we first produce a certain sheaf of algebras $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ over $\mathbb{S}$ (see Section 3.3) and then construct an action of $G_{0}$ on the corresponding sheaf of categories over $\mathbb{S}$ given by $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ (Section 5). If $(X,[\eta])$ is $\Spec A_{0}$ equipped with the natural restricted symplectic structure then $\QCoh_{h}$ is equivalent $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . We will call $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ the “twistor reduced Weyl algebra”.

Let us very briefly explain the construction of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . Namely, in the even-dimensional case one can identify $\Spec A_{0}$ with a subvariety in cotangent bundle of a similar Frobenius neighborhood $\Spec C$ , but of half the dimension. More precisely, $\Spec A_{0}$ is just a Frobenius-neighborhood of zero section in $T^{*}\Spec C$ . The sheaf of algebras $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is defined as the corresponding central reduction of twistor differential operators $\mathcal{D}_{\Spec C,\mathbb{S}}$ , see Section 3.3 and Definition 3.14 in particular. $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is a locally free sheaf of algebras on $\mathbb{S}$ with the fiber at $\{0\}\in\mathbb{S}$ is given by $A_{0}$ , and with restriction to $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ being a split Azumaya algebra: this way one can view $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ as a certain order in a matrix algebra over $\mathbb{S}$ .

In Section 5 we construct the desired $G_{0}$ -action on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . The key observation is that imposing certain properties on the action automatically makes it canonical. More precisely, in Theorem 1 we show that there is a unique $G_{0}$ -action on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ that restricts to the natural action of $G_{0}$ on $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ over $\{0\}\in\mathbb{S}$ and is trivial over $\{\infty\}\in\mathbb{S}$ . The proof of uniqueness crucially uses the description of automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ whose restriction to $\{0\}\in\mathbb{S}$ is trivial, which we establish in Section 3.6. The construction of the existence is quite elaborate and uses an auxiliary sheaf of algebras $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\flat}$ with a natural $G_{0}$ -action (see Section 3.7), as well as a certain $G_{0}$ -action on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{S}}}\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\flat,\op}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ constructed in [BV] in the formal neighborhood of 0. In Section 5.3 we also show that the $G_{0}$ -action on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ extends to a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}$ -action equivariant structure where $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ now acts non-trivially on $\mathbb{S}$ . This allows to descend $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ further to a sheaf of categories over $[\mathbb{S}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})]$ .

In Section 6 we discuss the proprties of the resulting sheaf of categories $\QCoh_{h}$ . In 6.1 we translate the defining properties of our $G_{0}$ -action on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ into defining properties for $\QCoh_{h}$ . In Section 6.2 we give a slightly finer construction in the presence of a $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action on $X$ that rescales the contact form $[\eta]$ with a weight coprime to $p$ . In this case one can descend $\QCoh_{h}$ further to the quotient stack $[(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{S})/\mathbb{G}_{m}]$ under the diagonal action, where $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ acts on $\mathbb{S}$ by rescaling with the same weight as above. In Section 6.3 we discuss the relation of $\QCoh_{h}$ with the Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{h}$ constructed by Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin. Finally, in Section 6.4 we also construct the canonical quantization of restricted Lagrangian subvarieties extending the work of Mundinger [Mu].

### 1.2. Properties of $\QCoh_{h}$ .

For simplicity, below we let $X$ be a smooth scheme over a field of characteristic $p>2$ . In this case $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq X^{(1)}$ , and $\QCoh_{h}$ is a sheaf of categories over $X^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S}$ ; thus for each scheme $T\rightarrow X^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S}$ over $X^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S}$ we obtain a category $\QCoh_{h}(T)$ . Let us summarize the nice properties of $\QCoh_{h}$ that we obtain in Section 6.

- (1) If we consider the $G_{0}$ -torsor $\pi\colon{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ of Darboux frames corresponding to $[\eta]$ then the pull-back $(\pi\times\id)^{*}\QCoh_{h}$ is equivalent to $(p_{2}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}){\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ , where $p_{2}\colon{\mathcal{M}}\times\mathbb{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ is the projection.

- (2) The global sections $\QCoh_{h}(X^{\prime}\times\{0\})$ on the fiber over $\{0\}\in\mathbb{S}$ are given by $\QCoh(X).$

- (3) In the case $H^{i}(X,{\mathcal{O}}_{X})=0$ for $i=1,2,3$ , we have an equivalence $\QCoh_{h}|_{X^{(1)}\times\widehat{\mathbb{S}}}\simeq O_{h}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ where $O_{h}$ is the distinguished Frobenius-constant quantization constructed in [BK].

- (4) $\QCoh_{h}$ is functorial in $(X,[\eta])$ . In particular, for any map $T\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ there is a natural $\mathcal{O}(T)$ -linear action of restricted Poisson automorphisms $\mathrm{Aut}((X,[\eta]))$ on the global sections $\QCoh_{h}(X^{(1)}\times T)$ .

- (5) The restriction of $\QCoh_{h}$ to $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times({\mathbb{S}}\backslash\{0\})$ is equivalent to ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ , where ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h}}$ is the central reduction of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ correponding to $[\eta]$ (see Construction 3.12).

- (6) The global sections $\QCoh_{h}(X^{\prime}\times\{\infty\})$ on the fiber over $\{\infty\}\in\mathbb{S}$ are given by $\QCoh(X^{\prime}).$

- (7) For a smooth Lagrangian subvariety $Y\subset X$ such that ${[\eta]|}_{Y}=0$ there exists a canonical flat object ${\mathcal{V}}_{Y^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S}}\in\QCoh_{h}(Y^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S})$ whose fiber over $Y^{(1)}\times\{0\}$ is given by $(\Omega_{Y}^{\dim Y})^{\tfrac{1-p}{2}}$ (considered as a quasi-coherent sheaf on $X$ ).

- (8) If $X$ is equipped with a $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action which rescales $[\eta]$ with a weight 1, then $\QCoh_{h}$ canonically descends further to the quotient stack $(X^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S})/\mathbb{G}_{m}$ where $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ acts diagonally.

#### Remark 1.1.

In the case $X=T^{*}Y$ and $\eta$ is the canonical 1-form on $T^{*}Y$ , the global sections $\QCoh_{h}(X^{(1)}\times\mathbb{S})$ can be alternatively described as the category of modules over the sheaf of twisted differential operators $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ .

Also, from the above picture one gets the following properties

- • $\QCoh_{h}(X^{(1)}\times\{0\})$ is given by the category of Higgs fields on $Y$ ;

- • $\QCoh_{h}(X^{(1)}\times\{1\})$ can be identified77 7 Using the Morita equivalence ${\mathcal{D}}_{X,[\eta]}\sim{\mathcal{D}}_{Y}$ ([BB]). with the category ${\mathcal{D}}_{Y}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ of $D$ -modules on $Y$ ;

- • $\QCoh_{h}(X^{(1)}\times\{\infty\})$ is the category of Higgs fields on the Frobenius twist $Y^{(1)}$ .

This resembles the construction of the twistor space due to Deligne and Simpson: namely, given a smooth projective variety $Y$ over $\mathbb{C}$ they construct a complex-analytic space $W\rightarrow{\mathbb{P}}^{1}$ whose fiber over $\lambda\in{\mathbb{P}}^{1}({\mathbb{C}})$ is the “moduli space” of $\lambda$ -connections on $Y$ . In particular, fibers $W_{0}$ , $W_{1}$ and $W_{\infty}$ over $0$ , $1$ and $\infty\in{\mathbb{P}}^{1}({\mathbb{C}})$ are given by

- • holomorphic Higgs fields on $Y$ ;

- • bundles with holomorphic flat connections on $Y$ ;

- • holomorphic Higgs fields on the complex conjugate $\overline{Y}$

correspondingly. This way the category $\QCoh_{h}$ can be considered as a categorified characteristic $p$ analogue of their construction. This motivates calling $\QCoh_{X,[\eta],h}$ the twistor category associated to $(X,[\eta])$ .

## 2. Differential geometry on pseudo-smooth schemes

### 2.1. Pseudo-smooth schemes

Let $B$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra. Following [BK] we consider the following notion.

#### Definition 2.1.

A finite-type $B$ -algebra $A$ is called pseudo-smooth if $\Omega^{1}_{A/B}$ is a locally free $A$ -module. A qcqs morphism $X\rightarrow S$ locally of finite type is called pseudo-smooth if $\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ is a locally free sheaf of finite type.

#### Remark 2.2.

In [BK], Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin call88 8 Strictly speaking they also assume that $A/B$ is flat and $B$ is Noetherian. such algebras quasi-regular. However, since terms quasi-regular and quasi-smooth are quite broadly used with a different meaning, we decided to change it to pseudo-smooth.

#### Example 2.3.

- (1) Smooth schemes are pseudo-smooth.

- (2) Let $A\coloneqq B[x]/x^{p}$ . Then $\Omega^{1}_{A/B}=A\cdot dx$ and $A$ is pseudo-smooth.

- (3) Let $Z\hookrightarrow S$ be a closed subscheme. Then $\Omega^{1}_{Z/S}=0$ and $Z$ is pseudo-smooth over $S$ .

#### Remark 2.4.

One might count Example 2.3(3) as a pathological one and impose flatness condition in Definition 2.1. This is relatively harmless for our goals: namely, pseudo-smooth schemes that will appear in main applications (e.g. quantizations of smooth schemes) will all be flat.

#### Remark 2.5.

Pseudo-smoothness is preserved under base change: namely, having a pseudo smooth $S$ -scheme $X\rightarrow S$ and a morphism $S^{\prime}\rightarrow S$ the base change $X_{S^{\prime}}=X\times_{S}S^{\prime}$ is pseudo smooth over $S^{\prime}$ . Indeed one has $\Omega^{1}_{X/S^{\prime}}=f^{*}\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ where $f\colon X_{S^{\prime}}\rightarrow X$ is the natural map.

#### Construction 2.6 (Reduced Frobenius: algebras).

Let $A$ be a $B$ -algebra. The absolute Frobenius map $F_{A}\colon A\rightarrow A$ factors naturally through the Frobenius twist $A^{(1)}\coloneqq A\otimes_{B,F_{B}}B$ :

$$ \textstyle{A\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{A}} \scriptstyle{W_{A/B}} \textstyle{A} \textstyle{A^{(1)}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{A/B}} $$

with $W_{A/B}\colon a\mapsto a\otimes 1\in A^{(1)}$ and $F_{A/B}\colon a\otimes b\mapsto a^{p}b\in A$ . The map $F_{A/B}$ is usually called the relative Frobenius; by construction it is $B$ -linear (while $F_{A}$ and $W_{A/B}$ are $F_{B}$ -linear). However, if $B$ or $A$ are not reduced one can factor $F_{A/B}$ even further. Namely, let $A^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\subset A$ be the image of $F_{A/B}$ : this is the $B$ -subalgebra in $A$ generated by $p$ -th powers $A^{p}$ , in other words $A^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\coloneqq B\cdot A^{p}\subset A$ . By definition, one has a natural surjection $F_{A}^{{int}}\colon A^{(1)}\twoheadrightarrow A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Moreover, we get a further factorization

$$ \textstyle{A\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{A}} \scriptstyle{W_{A/B}} \textstyle{A} \textstyle{A^{(1)}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{A/B}} \scriptstyle{F_{A}^{int}} \textstyle{A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} $$

We have $F_{A/B}=F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\circ F_{A}^{int}$ and we can put $W_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq F_{A}^{int}\circ W_{A/S}$ . We will call $F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and $F_{A}^{int}$ the reduced and intermediate Frobenii of $A$ correspondingly.

In the case when both $A$ and $B$ are reduced, $F_{A}^{int}$ is an isomorphism and so $F_{A/B}=F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . However, we will be primarily interested in the non-reduced setting, where $A^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ will turn out to be more relevant than $A^{(1)}$ .

#### Remark 2.7.

Let us try to motivate consideration of the reduced Frobenius as compared to the relative one. The main reason is that when $A$ is pseudo-smooth, $F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ still enjoys some properties that the relative Frobenius $F_{A/B}$ has if we assume that $A$ is actually smooth. For example, we will see further that under the pseudo-smoothness assumption (see Remark 2.39) $F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a finite faithfully flat map, which is no longer true for the relative Frobenius $F_{A/B}$ in this generality. This is illustrated well by the example of $A\coloneqq B[x]/x^{p}$ , where one has $A^{(1)}\simeq B[x]/x^{p}$ and where the relative Frobenius $F_{A/B}\colon B[x]/x^{p}\rightarrow B[x]/x^{p}$ is the unique $B$ -algebra map that sends $x$ to 0. This map is clearly not flat. On the other hand, $A^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\subset A$ is identified with $B\subset B[x]/x^{p}$ and the reduced Frobenius $F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon A^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow A$ is given by the above embedding which is indeed finite and faithfully flat.

#### Remark 2.8.

In [BK], for a pseudo-smooth $A$ it is claimed that $A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ can be identified with the tensor product $A^{p}\otimes_{B^{p}}B$ via the natural map $a^{p}\otimes b\mapsto a^{p}b$ . Unfortunately, this is not exactly true. Put $B\coloneqq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]$ and $A=B[t]/(t^{p}-x)$ . One checks easily that $\Omega^{1}_{A/B}\simeq A\cdot dt$ , and so $A$ is pseudo-smooth. On the other hand $B^{p}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x^{p}]$ , $A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq A^{p}\simeq B$ , and so the natural map $A^{p}\otimes_{B^{p}}B\rightarrow A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is identified with multiplication map $\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[x^{p}]}\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]\rightarrow\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]$ which is not an isomorphism.

#### Remark 2.9.

Let $X=\Spec A$ . By [Stacks, Tag0BR8], $F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq\Spec A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a universal homeomorphism. In particular, it induces an isomorphism of the underlying topological spaces. In fact all three schemes $X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow X^{(1)}\coloneqq\Spec A^{(1)}$ have the same underlying topological space and the difference between them is only seen on the level of sheaves of functions.

#### Construction 2.10 (Reduced Frobenius: schemes).

Given a base scheme $S$ and an $S$ -scheme $X$ , the construction $A\rightarrow A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ globalizes, producing an $S$ -scheme $X^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ . This is a scheme which has the same underlying topological space as the original $X$ and its Frobenius twist $X^{(1)}\coloneqq X\times_{S,F_{S}}S$ , but with the sheaf of functions given by $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\cdot\mathcal{O}_{S}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ . One has maps $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{X^{(1)}}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (given locally by $F_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and $F_{A}^{int}$ ) which induce a map $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and a closed embedding $F_{X}^{int}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow X^{(1)}$ . This way one can also view $X^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ as the schematic image of the relative Frobenius $F_{X/S}\colon X\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ inside the Frobenius twist $X^{(1)}\coloneqq X\times_{S,F_{S}}S$ . We will call $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and $F_{X}^{int}$ the reduced and intermediate Frobenii of $X$ ; both are morphisms of $S$ -schemes. We can also define a reduced twist map $W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow X$ (by globalizing $W_{A}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ ); this map is not a morphism of $S$ -schemes, instead it is $F_{S}$ -linear. One has relations $F_{X}^{int}\circ F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}=F_{X/S}$ and $W_{X/S}\circ F_{X}^{int}=W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

#### Example 2.11.

Assume $S=\Spec B$ .

- (1) Put $P\coloneqq B[x_{1},\ldots,x_{d}]$ with $\Spec P\simeq\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S}$ . Then $P^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq P^{p}\cdot B\simeq B[x_{1}^{p},\ldots,x_{d}^{p}]\subset P$ . On the other hand the Frobenius twist $P^{(1)}\coloneqq P\otimes_{B,F_{B}}B\simeq B[y_{1},\ldots,y_{d}]$ (with $y_{i}\coloneqq x_{i}\otimes 1$ ), and the relative Frobenius $F_{P/B}\colon P^{(1)}\rightarrow P$ is the unique $B$ -algebra map that sends $y_{i}$ to $x_{i}^{p}$ . We see that in this case the intermediate Frobenius $F_{\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S}}^{int}\colon(\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S})^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow(\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S})^{(1)}$ is an isomorphism.

- (2) Consider the unique surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow B$ of $B$ -algebras sending every $x_{i}$ to 0. It corresponds to the embedding $\{0\}_{S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S}$ of 0. Put

$$ Q\coloneqq B\otimes_{P,F^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}_{P}}P\simeq P/(x_{1}^{p},\ldots,x_{d}^{p}). $$

$X\coloneqq\Spec Q\hookrightarrow\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S}$ is the Frobenius neighborhood of 0: namely, $X\simeq\{0\}_{S}\times_{\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S},F^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{\mathbb{A}^{d}}}\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S}$ . We have $Q^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq Q^{p}\cdot B\simeq B\subset Q$ . However, $Q^{(1)}\coloneqq Q\otimes_{B,F_{B}}B\simeq B[y_{1},\ldots,y_{d}]/(y_{1}^{p},\ldots,y_{d}^{p})$ , and the intermidiate Frobenius $F_{Q}^{int}\colon Q^{(1)}\rightarrow Q^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq B$ sends $y_{i}$ to $x_{i}^{p}=0$ .

#### Remark 2.12.

Since $F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a universal homeomorphism, say by [Stacks, Tag 0BTY] it induces an equivalence of small étale sites $(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})_{\text{et}}\simeq X_{\text{et}}$ , by

$$ (U\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\in(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})_{\text{et}}\ \ \mapsto\ \ (X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}U\rightarrow X)\in X_{\text{et}}. $$

### 2.2. Restricted Lie algebras and Jacobson’s formula

Let $A$ be an associative ring such that $p\cdot A=0$ . For $a\in A$ denote by $\ad(a)\colon A\rightarrow A$ a map that sends $b\mapsto[a,b]=ab-ba$ .

If $A$ is commutative, given two elements $a,b\in A$ we have $(a+b)^{p}=a^{p}+b^{p}$ . This formula generalizes to the general non-commutative case as follows

#### Lemma 2.13 (Jacobson, [GD, Chapter II, §7, Proposition 3.2]).

Let $a,b\in A$ . Then

$$ (a+b)^{p}=a^{p}+b^{p}+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}L_{i}(a,b) $$

where $L_{i}(a,b)$ is a Lie polynomial described as $i^{-1}$ times the coefficient of $t^{i-1}$ in the expression $\ad(a+tb)^{p-1}(b)\in A[t]$ .

#### Remark 2.14.

In particular, $L_{1}(a,b)=\ad(a)^{p-1}(b)$ .

#### Remark 2.15.

For an element $a\in A$ denote by $\ad(a)\colon A\rightarrow A$ the commutator map $x\mapsto[a,x]$ . Note that $\ad(a)^{p}=\ad(a^{p})$ . Indeed, $\ad(a)=\ell(a)-r(a)$ where $\ell(a),r(a)\colon A\rightarrow A$ are left and right multiplications by $a$ correspondingly. Since $\ell(a)$ and $r(a)$ commute we have

$$ \ad(a)^{p}=(\ell(a)-r(a))^{p}=\ell(a)^{p}-r(a)^{p}=\ell(a^{p})-r(a^{p})=\ad(a^{p}). $$

We now remind the definition of a restricted Lie algebra.

#### Definition 2.16.

A restricted Lie algebra over a ring $B$ is given by a $B$ -module $L$ with a $B$ -linear Lie bracket $[-,-]$ and a restricted $p$ -power operation $-^{[p]}$ that are compatible in the following way:

- (1) $(bx)^{[p]}=b^{p}x^{[p]}$ for any $b\in B$ and $x\in L$ ;

- (2) $[x^{[p]},y]=\ad(x)^{p}(y)$ for any $x,y\in L$ ;

- (3) $(x+y)^{[p]}=x^{[p]}+y^{[p]}+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}L_{i}(x,y)$ , where $L_{i}(x,y)$ are the Lie polynomials from Lemma 2.13.

The definition of restricted Lie algebra is mainly motivated by the following example:

#### Example 2.17.

Let $A$ be an associative $B$ -algebra. Then by Lemma 2.13 and Remark 2.15, $A$ endowed with the Lie bracket given by commutator $[-,-]$ and the restricted structure $a^{[p]}\coloneqq a^{p}$ is a restricted Lie algebra.

Another natural source of examples of restricted Lie algebras is differential geometry in char $p$ (see Remark 2.19 below). In particular, Lie algebra of any group scheme $G$ is endowed with a natural restricted Lie algebra structure.

### 2.3. Crystalline differential operators

We essentially follow [BMR, Section 2], except we work in a relative and pseudo-smooth setting.

Let $X\rightarrow S$ be a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme. Let $\mathcal{T}_{X}\coloneqq\mathcal{T}_{X/S}$ be the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear differentiations of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ . We will ocasionally call (local) sections of $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ vector fields.

Denote $\Omega^{1}_{X}\coloneqq\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ . One has $\mathcal{T}_{X}\simeq(\Omega^{1}_{X})^{\vee}$ , and, since $X$ is pseudo-smooth, we get that $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ is a locally free $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -module of finite rank.

The sheaf $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ has a natural ( $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear) Lie-bracket given by commutator99 9 Namely, the commutator of two differentiations is again a differentiation. which endows it with the structure of a Lie algebroid over $X$ . Let $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ be the universal enveloping algebra of $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ . Explicitly, $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is generated over $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ by $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ with the relations given by $f_{1}\cdot f_{2}-f_{2}\cdot f_{1}=0$ for $f_{i}\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , $v\cdot f-f\cdot v=v(f)\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ for $v\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ and $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , and $v_{1}\cdot v_{2}-v_{2}\cdot v_{1}=[v_{1},v_{2}]\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ for $v_{i}\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ . A data of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -quasicoherent $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ -module is equivalent to what is usually called a “D-module” on $X$ : namely, a quasicoherent sheaf $\mathcal{E}$ endowed with a flat connection $\nabla\colon\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}\otimes\Omega^{1}_{X}$ .

#### Remark 2.18.

The algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ comes with a natural increasing “PBW-filtration” which is identified with the filtration by order of the differential operator. Namely, $\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq n}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is the $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -submodule locally generated by the image of the multiplication map $\underbrace{\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\ldots\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}\mathcal{T}_{X}}_{n}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_{X}$ . Note that since $[\mathcal{T}_{X},\mathcal{T}_{X}]\subset\mathcal{T}_{X}$ we have $[\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq i},\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq j}]\subset\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq i+j-1}$ . By a version of PBW-theorem for Lie algebroids ref one has a natural isomorphism

$$ \gr_{*}\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{T}_{X}. $$

Consequently, if we have a trivialization $\mathcal{T}_{X}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}^{d}$ given by a frame of vector fields $\partial_{1},\ldots,\partial_{d}$ we can decompose

$$ \mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq\oplus_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}\mathcal{O}_{X}\cdot\partial^{\alpha} $$

as a left $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -module. Here, for $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^{d}$ , $\partial^{\alpha}$ denotes the monomial $\partial_{1}^{\alpha_{1}}\ldots\partial_{d}^{\alpha_{d}}$ . In terms of this decomposition $\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq n}\simeq\oplus_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}\mathcal{O}_{X}\cdot\partial^{\alpha}$ with

$$ |\alpha|=\alpha_{1}+\ldots+\alpha_{d}\leq n. $$

#### Remark 2.19 (Restricted Lie algebra structure on $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ ).

In char $p$ , $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ is naturally a sheaf of restricted Lie algebras over $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ . Namely, note that the $p$ -th iterate of an $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear derivation $v\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ again defines a $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear derivation of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , which we will denote $v^{[p]}\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ . Since $v^{[p]}$ is equal to the image of $v^{p}$ in the $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear endomorphisms $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X})$ and the Lie bracket on $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ is induced by the commutator in $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X})$ , one sees from Example 2.17 that the relations in Definition 2.16 are satisfied.

The algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ naturally acts on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ by $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear endomorphisms: namely, $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ acts by multiplication, while $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ acts by the corresponding $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear derivations. Note that any $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear derivation acts by zero on all functions in $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}=\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\cdot\mathcal{O}_{S}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ . It follows that $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ lies in the center $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ , and so one can consider $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ as a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -algebras. By adjunction, from the identification $(F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}\mathcal{O}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , we get a map $\mathcal{O}_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\rightarrow Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ and this way we can consider $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ as a sheaf of algebras over $X^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ .

#### Remark 2.20.

By construction, the map $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is affine. Consequently, one has a monoidal equivalence of categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and quasi-coherent sheaves of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -modules on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . This then gives an equivalence of categories of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ -modules on $X$ and quasi-coherent $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ -modules on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

#### Remark 2.21.

Note that by base change, $\Omega^{1}_{X^{(1)}}\simeq W_{X/S}^{*}\Omega^{1}_{X}\coloneqq\Omega^{1}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X^{(1)}}$ . In particular, if $X$ is pseudo-smooth, then so is $X^{(1)}$ . We warn that this is not necessarily true for $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (see Remark 2.33).

Let us also define the appropriate variants of twisted tangent and cotangent bundles.

#### Construction 2.22 (Twisted tangent and cotangent bundles).

For the usual Frobenius twist, one can consider $\Omega^{1}_{X^{(1)}}\simeq\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X^{(1)}}$ and $\mathcal{T}_{X^{(1)}}\simeq W_{X/S}^{*}\mathcal{T}_{X}\coloneqq\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X^{(1)}}$ . Analogously, we define the (reduced Frobenius) twisted tangent and cotangent bundles $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq W_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\mathcal{T}_{X}\coloneqq\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ and $\Omega_{X}^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\coloneqq\Omega_{X}^{1}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ (here the map $\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ sends $f\mapsto f^{p}$ ). One has $\Omega_{X}^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq(\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{\vee}$ . We warn that it is no longer necessarily true that $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (resp. $\Omega_{X}^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ ) is isomorphic to $\mathcal{T}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ (resp. $\Omega^{1}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ ), e.g. since $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ can happen to be not smooth. Nevertheless there is still some natural compatibility (see Corollary 2.24).

For a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on a scheme $X$ let $\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\coloneqq\Spec_{X}\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{E}^{\vee}$ be the total space of $\mathcal{E}$ . In the case $\mathcal{E}$ is $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ or $\Omega^{1}_{X}$ we denote it by $TX$ and $T^{*}\!X$ correspondingly. We denote by $\mathcal{E}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq W_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\mathcal{E}\simeq\mathcal{E}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ the pull-back of $\mathcal{E}$ to $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

#### Lemma 2.23.

One has a natural isomorphism

$$ \mathrm{Tot}_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\mathcal{E}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})=\left(\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\right)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

#### Proof.

Note that $\mathrm{Tot}_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\mathcal{E}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\simeq\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\times_{X}X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ under the map $W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow X$ . Indeed, $\Sym_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}^{*}(\mathcal{E}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\simeq(\Sym_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}^{*}\mathcal{E})\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and the isomorphism is obtained by taking $\Spec_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ of both sides. By taking $W_{\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon\left(\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\right)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})$ and the projection $\left(\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\right)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ we obtain a map

$$ \left(\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\right)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\mathrm{Tot}_{X}(\mathcal{E})\times_{X}X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\mathrm{Tot}_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\mathcal{E}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}). $$

To check that it is an isomorphism we can work locally on $X$ and $S$ . So we can assume $X=\Spec A$ , $Y=\Spec B$ and $\mathcal{E}$ is trivial. Then we need to check that the natural map

$$ A[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}]\otimes_{A}A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow(A[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}])^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}} $$

given by $f\otimes s\mapsto f^{p}s$ is an isomorphism. But it is clear that the right hand side is the polynomial ring on $x_{1}^{p},\ldots,x_{n}^{p}$ over $A^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and so this map is indeed an isomorphism. ∎

Plugging $\mathcal{E}$ to be $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ or $\Omega^{1}_{X}$ we get

#### Corollary 2.24.

One has isomorphisms

$$ \mathrm{Tot}_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\simeq(TX)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\text{ and }\mathrm{Tot}_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\Omega_{X}^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})\simeq(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

#### Construction 2.25 ( $p$ -curvature map).

Let $X$ be a smooth $S$ -scheme. Consider the map $\theta\coloneqq\mathcal{T}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_{X}$ of sheaves on $X$ given by the following formula

$$ v\mapsto\theta(v)\coloneqq v^{p}-v^{[p]}, $$

where $-^{[p]}$ is the restricted power (see Remark 2.19). We claim that

- • $\theta$ is additive: $\theta(v_{1}+v_{2})-(\theta(v_{1})+\theta(v_{2}))=0$ ;

- • $\theta$ is Frobeinus-linear: $\theta(fv)-f^{p}\cdot\theta(v)=0$ ;

- • $\theta(v)$ lies in the center $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ for any $v\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ : $[\theta(v),f]=[\theta(v),w]=0$ for any $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $w\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ .

Indeed, note that $\theta(v)\in\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq p}$ and that its image in $\gr_{p}\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq\Sym^{p}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{T}_{X})$ is $v^{p}$ . It is easy1010 10 For all cases except $[\theta(v),w]$ this follows from the fact that the associated graded of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is commutative. For $[\theta(v),w]$ one can use that $[-,w]$ induces a derivation of $\gr_{*}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ by sending $x\in\gr_{i}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ to the class of $[\tilde{x},w]\in\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq i}$ in $\gr_{i}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ , and that any derivation is 0 on the $p$ -th power $v^{p}$ . to see that all expressions above have 0 image in $\gr_{p}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ , and so belong to $\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq p-1}$ . Thus, by Lemma 2.26 below, they are zero if and only of their images in $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X})$ are. However, $\theta(v)$ acts by 0 on any function $f$ in $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ since by definition $v^{[p]}$ acts as $v^{p}$ , and so the image of all of the expressions above in $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X})$ is identically 0.

This way we obtain a map

$$ \theta^{\prime}\colon\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\rightarrow Z(\mathcal{D}_{X}) $$

of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}$ -modules. Since $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ is in fact an $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\cdot\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -algebra we can extend this to a map $\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , or in other words a map of sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$

$$ \theta\colon\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}). $$

which we call the “ $p$ -curvature map”.

#### Lemma 2.26.

Let $X$ be smooth over $S$ . Then the natural $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -linear action of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ induces an embedding $\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq p-1}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X})$ .

#### Proof.

The statement is Zariski-local, so we can assume that we have an étale map $f\colon X\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{n}_{S}$ given by functions $f_{1},\ldots,f_{n}$ . Let $z_{1},\ldots,z_{n}$ be the coordinates on $\mathbb{A}^{n}$ . We have an isomorphism $\mathcal{T}_{X}\simeq f^{*}\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{A}^{n}_{S}}$ and can consider the trivialization of $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ given by $\partial_{i}\coloneqq f^{-1}(\partial_{z_{i}})$ . We have $f_{i}=f^{*}(z_{i})$ and this way $\partial_{i}(f_{j})=\delta_{ij}$ . $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ is trivial with basis $\partial_{i}$ , $i=1,\ldots,n$ where $n=\rk(\Omega^{1}_{X})$ . Let $D\in\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq p-1}$ ; by Remark 2.18 it can be written as a sum

$$ D=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}g_{\alpha}\cdot\partial^{\alpha} $$

where $g_{\alpha}\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $\alpha=(\alpha_{1},\ldots,\alpha_{n})$ is such that $|\alpha|\leq p-1$ . Take a maximal $\alpha$ with respect to the lexicographic order on $\mathbb{N}^{d}$ such that $g_{\alpha}\neq 0$ ; then it is easy to check that $D(f_{1}^{\alpha_{1}}\ldots f_{n}^{\alpha_{n}})=\alpha_{1}!\ldots\alpha_{n}!\cdot g_{\alpha}$ , which is non-zero since all $\alpha_{i}<p$ . ∎

Recall the twisted tangent and cotangent bundles (Construction 2.22 $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ ). By Corollary 2.24 we have

$$ (T^{*}X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Spec_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}) $$

be the total space of $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ . The natural projection $(T^{*}X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is affine and so one has an equivalence of categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and quasi-coherent $\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\mathcal{T}_{X{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ -modules on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . The map $\theta$ above extends to a map of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -algebras

$$ \theta\colon\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\!\mathcal{T}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}), $$

and this way $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ defines a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

Then, following [BMR] (or rather [OV, Section 2.1] in the relative setting) we have the following structural result for $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ .

#### Proposition 2.27.

Let $X$ be a smooth $S$ -scheme. Then

- (1) The $p$ -curvature map (defined in the end of Section 2.3)

$$ \theta\colon\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\mathcal{T}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}) $$

is an isomorphism.

- (2) The sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ defined by $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is an Azumaya algebra of rank $2p^{\dim_{S}X}$ .

#### Example 2.28.

Assume that $S=\Spec B$ is affine and that $X\coloneqq\mathbb{A}^{d}_{S}$ with coordinates $z_{1},\ldots,z_{d}$ . In this case global sections of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ are given by the Weyl algebra

$$ W_{d}(B)\coloneqq B\langle z_{1},\ldots,z_{d},\partial_{z_{1}},\ldots,\partial_{z_{d}}\rangle/([z_{i},z_{j}]=[\partial_{z_{i}},\partial_{z_{j}}]=0,[\partial_{z_{j}},z_{i}]=\delta_{ij}). $$

The $p$ -th power $\partial_{z_{i}}^{p}$ acts by zero on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , so $\partial_{z_{i}}^{[p]}=0$ and $\theta(\partial_{x_{i}})=\partial_{z_{i}}^{p}$ . Then proposition 2.27 tells us that the center $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ is isomorphic to the polynomial ring $B[z_{i}^{p},\partial_{z_{i}}^{p}]\subset\mathcal{D}_{X}$ and that $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is an Azumaya algebra over it.

We finish with some remarks that will be useful in the next section:

#### Remark 2.29.

Consider the homomorphism $\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\mathcal{T}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ sending $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ to 0. It corresponds to the embedding of the zero section $i_{0}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Then the pull-back $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}\coloneqq i_{0}^{*}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ is an Azumaya algebra on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ which is canonically split. Indeed, $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ is a vector bundle of rank $p^{\dim_{S}X}$ and $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\subset Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ acts on it by 0 (since $v^{[p]}$ by definition acts as $v^{p}$ ): so the action of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ on $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ factors through $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}$ . Comparing the ranks we get that $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ is a splitting bundle for $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}$ , and so

$$ \mathcal{D}_{X,0}\simeq\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}). $$

#### Remark 2.30 (Cartier’s equivalence).

From the above remark one gets an equivalence of categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}$ -modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . The corresponding pair of qausi-inverse functors is given by $-\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal{D}_{X,0}}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X},-)$ . Under this equivalence the $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}$ -module $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ corresponds to $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

#### Remark 2.31.

Let $\mathcal{I}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ be a quasicoherent sheaf of ideals that is invariant under the action of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ . Note that $F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ is affine, so the pushforward $F_{X*}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ is exact, and for any quasicoherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ the map $(F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{F})\rightarrow\mathcal{F}$ is an equivalence. The pushforward $\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}(\mathcal{I})$ then gives a sub- $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}$ -module of $\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ which by the equivalence in Remark 2.30 is necessarily of the form $\mathcal{J}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}\subset\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ for some ideal $\mathcal{J}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Under the equivalence of categories between quasicoherent modules over $\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ the module $\mathcal{J}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{F}_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ exactly corresponds to $(F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{*}\mathcal{J}$ , and so we get that $\mathcal{I}\simeq F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}(\mathcal{J})$ for some ideal $\mathcal{J}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

### 2.5. Local structure of a pseudo-smooth scheme

The goal of this section is to give a local description of a general pseudo-smooth scheme which will allow us to make a reduction to smooth case. We start with the following lemma:

#### Lemma 2.32.

Let $Y$ be a smooth $S$ -scheme, and let $Z\subset Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ be a subscheme. Then the preimage $(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)=Z\times_{Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}Y\subset Y$ is a pseudo-smooth scheme.

#### Proof.

Let $\mathcal{J}\subset\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ be the sheaf of ideals defining $Z$ . Then $\mathcal{I}\coloneqq F_{Y}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}(\mathcal{J})\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ is the sheaf of ideals defining $X\coloneqq(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)$ . Note that $\mathcal{I}$ is locally generated by elements in $\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq(F_{Y}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})^{-1}\mathcal{O}_{Y{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ . Let $i\colon X\rightarrow Y$ be the corresponding embedding. We have an exact sequence

$$ \ldots\rightarrow i^{-1}(\mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}^{2})\xrightarrow{d}i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}\twoheadrightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X}\rightarrow 0 $$

of sheaves on $X$ where the left map is induced by the map that sends $[f]\in\mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}^{2}$ to $df\in\Omega^{1}_{Y}$ . However, for any $f\in\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ we have $df=0$ . Since $\mathcal{I}$ is locally generated by elements in $\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ we get that the map $d$ above is equal to 0 and so $\Omega^{1}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}$ . ∎

#### Remark 2.33.

We claim that in the above case the reduced Frobenius twist $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is given by $Z$ . Indeed, $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ (or rather $i_{*}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ ) is described as the reduction $\mathcal{O}_{Y}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\!/\mathcal{J}$ . Indeed, $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ is the subalgebra in $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ generated by $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ , which is easily seen to be isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\!/\mathcal{J}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{Z}$ . Moreover, this way the correponding embedding $i^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is identified with the original $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Consequently, we also see that the commutative diagram

$$ \textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} \scriptstyle{i} \textstyle{Z\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{i^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} \textstyle{Y\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} \textstyle{Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} $$

is in fact a fiber square. In particular, $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a finite locally free map of degree $p^{\dim_{S}Y}$ .

Note that $Z$ here was an arbitrary closed scheme of $Y$ ; in particular, it could be very singular.

#### Remark 2.34.

Recall that in the course of proof of Lemma 2.32 we showed that $i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}\simeq\Omega^{1}_{X}$ via the natural map. It then formally follows that $i^{*}\Omega^{j}_{Y}\simeq\Omega^{j}_{X}$ for all $j\geq 0$ . By considering the commutative diagram

$$ \textstyle{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} \scriptstyle{i^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} \textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{i} \textstyle{Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{W_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}} \textstyle{Y} $$

it also follows that the natural map $i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\Omega^{j,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{Y}\rightarrow\Omega^{j,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ induced by the identification $i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\circ W_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}=W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\circ i$ is an isomorphism for any $j\geq 0$ .

In fact, all pseudo-smooth schemes Zariski-locally look like Frobenius neighborhoods in smooth schemes:

#### Proposition 2.35.

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme. Then Zariski-locally it is of the form $(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)=Z\times_{Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}Y\subset Y$ with $Y$ smooth over $S$ and $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed subscheme (see Lemma 2.32).

#### Proof.

Let $x\in X$ be a point. We will show that there is a neighborhood of $x$ of the form above.

Since $X$ is locally of finite type, passing to an open we can assume that there is an embedding $i\colon X\hookrightarrow\mathbb{A}^{n}$ ; the natural map $i^{*}\colon i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{\mathbb{A}^{n}}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X}$ is a surjection. Let $\mathcal{I}\subset\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}^{n}}$ be the ideal defining $X$ . As before, we have an exact sequence

$$ \ldots\rightarrow i^{-1}(\mathcal{I}/\mathcal{I}^{2})\xrightarrow{d}i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{\mathbb{A}^{n}}\xrightarrow{i^{*}}\Omega^{1}_{X}\rightarrow 0. $$

Since $X$ is pseudo-smooth, the kernel of $i^{*}$ is a vector bundle. Let $d\coloneqq\rk H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X})$ . After passing to a neighborhood $U$ of $x$ in $\mathbb{A}^{n}$ we can assume that $\Ker(i^{*})$ is a trivial vector bundle with basis given by differentials $df_{1},\ldots,df_{n-d}$ of $(n-d)$ functions $f_{1},\ldots,f_{n-d}\in\mathcal{I}$ . Consider the map $s\colon\mathcal{O}_{U}^{\oplus n-d}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{U}$ defined by $(n-d)$ sections $df_{1},\ldots,df_{n-d}$ . The support of its kernel is a closed subset which doesn’t intersect $X$ (and in particular doesn’t contain $x$ ) thus considering the complement we can assume that $s$ is an embedding. Moreover, the dimension of the stalk of the cokernel is an upper-semicontinuous function bounded below by $n-(n-d)=d$ . Since it is equal to $d$ on $X$ we see that it is also equal to $d$ on some neighborhood, and so restriction of the cokernel to this neighborhood is a vector bundle of rank $d$ . Shrinking the open further we can assume that $\Omega^{1}_{U}$ is trivial with basis given by differentials $df_{1},\ldots,df_{n-d},dg_{1},\ldots,dg_{d}$ (with $f_{i}$ ’s being the functions we considered before, and $g_{i}$ ’s some other functions).

Now, let $i_{Y}\colon Y\hookrightarrow U$ be the subscheme defined by $\mathcal{I}_{Y}\coloneqq(f_{1},\ldots,f_{n-d})\subset\mathcal{I}$ . Then we claim that the map $q\colon Y\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{d}$ given by $g_{1},\ldots,g_{d}$ is étale. Indeed, one can realize $Y$ as a subscheme in $U\times\mathbb{A}^{d}\subset\mathbb{A}^{n}\times\mathbb{A}^{d}$ cut out by equations $f_{1}=\ldots=f_{n-d}=t_{1}-g_{1}=\ldots=t_{d}-g_{d}=0$ where $t_{i}$ ’s are coordinates on $\mathbb{A}^{d}$ . Since $df_{1},\ldots,df_{n-d},dg_{1},\ldots,dg_{d}$ are linearly independent over $\mathcal{O}_{U}$ fiberwise, the Jacobian of this system of equations (relative to $\mathbb{A}^{d}$ ) is a unit, and so projection to $\mathbb{A}^{d}$ is étale.

This way we get that $Y$ is in fact smooth over $S$ . Let $\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\subset\mathcal{O}_{Y}$ be the ideal defining $i_{X}\colon X\hookrightarrow Y$ . We have an exact sequence

$$ \ldots\rightarrow i^{-1}(\mathcal{I}^{\prime}/\mathcal{I}^{\prime 2})\xrightarrow{d}i^{*}_{X}\Omega^{1}_{Y}\xrightarrow{i_{X}^{*}}\Omega^{1}_{X}\rightarrow 0. $$

However, note that the map $i_{X}^{*}$ is now an isomorphism. Indeed, $i_{X}^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}$ is exactly the quotient of $i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{U}$ by $df_{i}$ , which are spanning the kernel of $i^{*}_{X}$ . Thus, we get that the map $d$ is 0, or, in other words, that $d(\mathcal{I}^{\prime})\subset\mathcal{I}^{\prime}$ . This is equivalent to $\mathcal{I}^{\prime}$ being invariant under the action of $\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ , from which it follows by Remark 2.31 that $\mathcal{I}^{\prime}\simeq F_{Y}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\mathcal{J}$ for some $\mathcal{J}\subset\mathcal{O}_{Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ . Then, putting $Z\subset\mathcal{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ to be the subscheme defined by $\mathcal{J}$ we exactly get that $X\simeq(F_{Y}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})^{-1}(Z)$ . ∎

Proposition 2.35 allows to extend the discussion in Section 2.4 to the pseudo-smooth setting. We start with an extension of Lemma 2.26:

#### Corollary 2.36.

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth scheme over $S$ . Then the natural map

$$ \mathcal{D}_{X,\leq p-1}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X}) $$

induced by the action of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ is an embedding.

#### Proof.

The statement is local, so we can assume that $X=(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)\hookrightarrow Y$ for a closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ in smooth scheme. We can also assume that $Y$ has an étale map $f\colon Y\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{n}$ . Let $\partial_{i}$ and $f_{i}$ be as in the proof of Lemma 2.26. Let $i\colon X\rightarrow Y$ be the embedding. Recall (see proof of Lemma 2.32) that $i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^{1}_{X}$ , and, consequently, $\mathcal{T}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\mathcal{T}_{Y}$ . Let $\partial_{i}^{\prime}\coloneqq i^{-1}(\partial_{i})\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ and let $f_{i}^{\prime}\coloneqq i^{*}(f_{i})\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ . We have $\partial_{i}^{\prime}(f_{j}^{\prime})=\delta_{ij}$ . The same argument as in Lemma 2.26 then shows that for any $D\in\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq p-1}$ there is a function $g\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ such that $D(g)\neq 0$ . ∎

#### Construction 2.37 ( $p$ -curvature map in the pseudo-smooth setting).

As in the smooth case, consider the map $\theta\coloneqq\mathcal{T}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_{X}$ of sheaves on $X$ given by the following formula

$$ v\mapsto\theta(v)\coloneqq v^{p}-v^{[p]}. $$

Using Corollary 2.36 in place of Lemma 2.26 as in Construction 2.25 one shows that

- • $\theta$ is additive: $\theta(v_{1}+v_{2})-(\theta(v_{1})+\theta(v_{2}))=0$ ;

- • $\theta$ is Frobeinus-linear: $\theta(fv)-f^{p}\cdot\theta(v)=0$ ;

- • $\theta(v)$ lies in the center $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ for any $v\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ : $[\theta(v),f]=[\theta(v),w]=0$ for any $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $w\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ .

This way we obtain a map

$$ \theta^{\prime}\colon\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\rightarrow Z(\mathcal{D}_{X}) $$

of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}$ -modules. Since $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ is in fact an $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\cdot\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -algebra we can extend this to a map $\mathcal{T}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , or, equivalently, a map of sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$

$$ \theta\colon\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}). $$

which we still call the “ $p$ -curvature map”.

#### Corollary 2.38.

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth scheme over $S$ . As before, consider $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Spec_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})$ .

- (1) The map $\theta\colon\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ induces an isomorphism

$$ \theta\colon\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\xrightarrow{\sim}Z(F_{X*}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{D}_{X}). $$

- (2) $F_{X*}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ , considered as a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , is an Azumaya algebra of rank1111 11 A priori this is a locally constant function on $X$ . $p^{2\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ .

#### Proof.

Both statements are local (e.g. in Zariski topology) and so we can assume $X\simeq(F_{Y}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})^{-1}(Z)$ where $Y$ is smooth over $S$ and $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed subscheme. In this case, $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is a central reduction of $\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ via an embedding $T^{*}Y^{(1)}|_{Z}\hookrightarrow T^{*}Y^{(1)}\simeq(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . More precisely, let $i\colon X\hookrightarrow Y$ be the embedding. Following the proof of Lemma 2.32 in this situation we have isomorphisms $\Omega^{1}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}$ , and consequently, $\mathcal{T}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\mathcal{T}_{Y}$ . By naturality, the latter is an isomorphism of Lie algebroids, and induces an isomorphism $\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ . Also

$$ \Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{O}_{Z} $$

and so $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ can be identified with the restriction of $(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ to $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Moreover, if we denote by $i_{Z}\colon Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ the corresponding embedding, applying $F_{X*}$ we get

$$ F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}(i^{*}\mathcal{D}_{Y})\simeq i_{Z}^{*}F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}\simeq F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{O}_{Z}\simeq F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\mathcal{O}_{(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}, $$

where in the last isomorphism we considered $F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ as an Azumaya algebra over $(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Thus we get that $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ as a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a restriction of an Azumaya algebra, and as such is an Azumaya algebra itself. Its center then also is necessarily isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . ∎

#### Remark 2.39.

From the proof of Proposition 2.35 it also follows that $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a finite faithfully flat map of degree $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ . Indeed, it is locally obtained as a base change of relative Frobenius for a smooth scheme $Y$ of (relative) dimension $\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}$ (see Remark 2.33).

### 2.6. De Rham complex and Cartier operation

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth scheme over $S$ . Put $r\coloneqq\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}$ ; this is a locally constant function on $X$ . Consider the de Rham complex

$$ \mathrm{dR}_{X}\coloneqq\left[0\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X}\rightarrow\ldots\rightarrow\Omega^{r}_{X}\rightarrow 0\right]{:} $$

this is a complex of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -modules on $X$ with differential given by the (relative) de Rham differential. Since the relative de Rham differential is $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\cdot B$ -linear, the pushforward $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ defines a complex of coherent sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

Let $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{*}\coloneqq\mathcal{H}^{*}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X})$ denote the sheaf cohomology algebra of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ . Recall the notation $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\coloneqq W_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\Omega^{1}_{X}$ . One can define the inverse Cartier morphism

$$ C^{-1}\colon\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\!(\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X})\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{*} $$

as follows. Namely in degree 0 it is given by $(F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}\colon\mathcal{O}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow F_{X*}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , while in degree 1 locally one sends $(W_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})^{-1}(df)\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ to $[f^{p-1}df]\in\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{1}$ . By a standard computation the latter gives a well-defined additive map to $\mathcal{H}^{1}_{\mathrm{dR},X}$ , which is $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -linear. For higher degrees $C^{-1}$ uniquely extends by multiplicativity.

The classical result of Cartier states that $C^{-1}$ is an equivalence if $X$ over $S$ is smooth. This remains true in the pseudo-smooth setting as well.

#### Proposition 2.40.

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme. Then the inverse Cartier map is an isomorphism.

#### Proof.

We deduce the statement from the smooth case. The statement is Zariski local, so we can assume $X=(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)$ is as in Lemma 2.32 (so $Y$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ ). In this case $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq Z$ . Let $i\colon X\hookrightarrow Y$ and $i^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . By Remarks 2.33, 2.34 and base change, $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ can be naturally identified with $i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{Y}$ . By Cartier isomorphism in the smooth case, the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},Y}^{*}$ are isomorphic to $\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{Y}$ ; in particular, they are vector bundles and thus are flat over $\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . From this and Remark 2.34 we get that

$$ \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{*}\simeq\mathcal{H}^{*}(i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{Y})\simeq i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},Y}^{*}\simeq i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}(\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{Y})\simeq\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}.\qed $$

Let $C$ be the inverse to $C^{-1}$ . In each degree $i$ , $C$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal{H}^{i}_{\mathrm{dR},X}\simeq\Omega^{i,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ which we can precompose with the projection $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{i}_{X,cl}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{H}^{i}_{\mathrm{dR},X}$ from the closed $i$ -forms. We will call the resulting map $\mathsf{C}^{i}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{i}_{X,cl}\twoheadrightarrow\Omega^{i,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ the Cartier operation. For $i=1$ one gets a short exact sequence

$$ 0\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}/\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\xrightarrow{d}F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\xrightarrow{\mathsf{C}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow 0, $$

of sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ where the term on the left is identified with the exact 1-forms via $d$ .

#### Remark 2.41.

The map $\mathsf{C}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ dually induces a map $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\otimes F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ which lifts the pairing map $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\otimes\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Substituting a local section $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ we obtain the corresponding “contraction” maps

$$ \widetilde{\iota_{\xi}}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\ \ \text{ and }\ \ \iota_{\xi}\colon\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

Following [BK], we have the following explicit formula for $\widetilde{\iota_{\xi}}$ . Namely, given a closed 1-form $\omega\in\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ and a vector field $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ (giving a section $\xi^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\coloneqq(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\xi)\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ ) one has the following formula
