$$ \widetilde{\iota_{\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\mathsf{C}(\omega))=\langle\xi^{[p]},\omega\rangle-\xi^{p-1}(\langle\xi,\omega\rangle) $$

for the corresponding contraction.

### 2.7. Line bundles with connection and Milne’s exact sequence

Let $(\mathcal{E},\nabla)$ , with $\nabla\colon\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}\otimes\Omega^{1}_{X}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf with flat connection on a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme $X$ . The connection $\nabla$ induces a map $\mathcal{D}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{E})$ , whose restriction to $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ factors through the subalgebra of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -linear endomorphisms $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})^{\nabla^{\prime}=0}\subset\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{E})$ that are flat with respect to the natural connection1212 12 Here the connection $\nabla^{\prime}$ on $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ is given by $(\nabla^{\prime}(\psi))(s)\coloneqq\nabla(\psi(s))-\psi(\nabla(s)$ for $s\in\mathcal{E}$ and $\psi\in\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ . Thus an endomorphism $\psi\in\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ is flat with respect to $\nabla^{\prime}$ if and only if it commutes with the action of $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ induced by $\nabla$ . on $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ . Indeed, central elements commute both with multiplication on functions and action by vector fields.

#### Construction 2.42 ( $p$ -curvature map for line bundles).

Let $\mathcal{E}\coloneqq\mathcal{L}$ in $(\mathcal{E},\nabla)$ be a line bundle. In this case, the endomorphism sheaf $(\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{L}),\nabla^{\prime})$ with its natural connection is given by $(\mathcal{O}_{X},d)$ . In particular, $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{L})^{\nabla^{\prime}=0}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ is given by $\ker d$ , which is identified with $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ by Proposition 2.40. Using the $p$ -curvature map (2.2) we obtain a map of sheaves $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , or, in other words, a section of $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ , which we will denote $\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L},\nabla)\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ . It is not hard to see from the definition (and the way $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\subset Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ acts on the tensor product), that

$$ \mathsf{c}_{p}((\mathcal{L}_{1},\nabla_{1})\otimes(\mathcal{L}_{2},\nabla_{2}))=\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L}_{1},\nabla_{1})+\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L}_{2},\nabla_{2}). $$

If we are given a trivialization $\mathcal{L}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , $\nabla$ can be written in the form $d+\alpha$ for some closed 1-form $\alpha\in\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ . Restricting to line bundles of this form we get a map of sheaves

$$ \mathsf{c}_{p}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X},\ \ \ \ \mathsf{c}_{p}\colon\alpha\mapsto\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha). $$

Since $(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha_{1})\otimes(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha_{2})\simeq(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2})$ the above map is a map of sheaves of abelian groups.

#### Remark 2.43.

One has an explicit formula for the map $\mathsf{c}_{p}$ in terms of the Cartier operation. Namely, given $\alpha\in\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ let’s compute the pairing $\langle\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha)\rangle$ for any $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ , $\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\in(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\xi)\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ : this will define $\mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha)$ uniquely. By definition, we need to compute the action of $\theta(\xi)=\xi^{p}-\xi^{[p]}$ on line bundle $(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha)$ . This is given by

$$ (\xi+\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle)^{p}-\xi^{[p]}-\langle\xi^{[p]},\alpha\rangle=\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle^{p}-\langle\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\mathsf{C}(\alpha)\rangle\in\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X}) $$

where for the equality we used that $\xi^{p}-\xi^{[p]}$ acts by 0 on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , formula (2.4) and also Jacobson’s formula. Note that $\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle^{p}=(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle)=\langle\xi^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}},\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rangle$ , where $\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}\alpha$ . This gives

$$ \mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha)=\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}-\mathsf{C}(\alpha). $$

We now consider a non-commutative counterpart of the above $p$ -curvature map.

#### Construction 2.44 (Central reductions of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ associated to 1-forms).

Let $\alpha\in H^{0}(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X})$ be a global section. Let $i_{\alpha}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ be the graph of $\alpha$ . Under the identification $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Spec_{X}\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , the image $\Gamma_{\alpha}=\im(i_{\alpha})\subset(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ of $i_{\alpha}$ is defined by the sheaf of ideals generated by linear expressions

$$ \mathcal{I}_{\alpha}\coloneqq(\xi-\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle)_{\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\subset\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

We denote by $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}\coloneqq i_{\alpha}^{*}(F_{X*}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ the corresponding pull-back of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ considered as a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . For any $\alpha$ the sheaf $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ defines an Azumaya algebra over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ of rank $p^{2\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ .

#### Construction 2.45 (Line bundles with connection vs splittings.).

Suppose we are given a line bundle with flat connection $(\mathcal{L},\nabla)$ and put $\alpha\coloneqq\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L},\nabla)$ . Then by definition of $\mathsf{c}_{p}$ we have that $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ acts on $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}$ by $\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle\in\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . It follows that the action of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ on $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}$ induced by $\nabla$ factors through $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ . Moreover, by Remark 2.39 $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}$ is a vector bundle of rank $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and thus is a splitting bundle for $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ : namely, $\nabla$ induces an isomorphism

$$ \nabla\colon\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}). $$

Vice versa, let $\mathcal{E}$ be a splitting bundle $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ -module on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Then $\mathcal{E}$ is a vector bundle of rank $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ . However $\mathcal{E}$ is also a quasi-coherent $F_{X*}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -module (with the action via the composition $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha})$ and so comes as a pushforward $(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\mathcal{F}$ of some quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ . Since $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a finite locally free map of degree $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ the only option is that $\mathcal{F}\simeq(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\mathcal{E})$ is a line bundle. The action of $\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ on $\mathcal{F}$ induces a natural flat connection, whose $p$ -curvature is given by $\alpha$ . Moreover, isomorphisms between two line bundles $(\mathcal{L}_{1},\nabla_{1})$ and $(\mathcal{L}_{2},\nabla_{2})$ with the same $p$ -curvature $\alpha$ exactly correspond to isomorphisms between the corresponding $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ -modules $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}_{1}$ and $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}_{2}$ . In particular, any two such line bundles a étale (and, in fact even Zariski) locally isomorphic.

This gives an equivalence of two groupoids: line bundles with flat connection on $X$ with $p$ -curvature $\alpha$ , and splitting bundles1313 13 Here an object is given by a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ together with an isomorphism $\gamma\colon\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}\simeq\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\mathcal{E})$ , and morphisms are isomorphisms of vector bundles that preserve this data. for $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ correspondingly.

Consider the map $d\log\colon\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ of étale sheaves on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ sending $f$ to $df/f$ . It induces a map of étale sheaves $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

#### Proposition 2.46.

There is a short exact sequence of étale sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$

$$ 0\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}/(\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{\times}\xrightarrow{d\log}F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\xrightarrow{\mathsf{c}_{p}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow 0, $$

where $\mathsf{c}_{p}$ is the map from Construction 2.42.

#### Proof.

The idea is to use the equivalence of groupoids described in Construction 2.45. First of all, the kernel of $d\log\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ is given by the intersection of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}$ and $\ker d\subset F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ . The latter is isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ by Proposition 2.40, so the intersection is exactly $(\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{\times}$ . This shows exactness from the left. To show that $\mathsf{c}_{p}$ is surjective, for any local section $\alpha\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ it is enough to show that étale locally on $X$ there is a line bundle with $p$ -curvature given by (the corresponding pull-back of) $\alpha$ . By the above this is equivalent to finding a splitting bundle for the Azumaya algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ , which is always possible étale locally. It remains to show the exactness in the middle. Let $\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}$ be two closed forms on an étale open $U\rightarrow X$ such that $\mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha_{1})=\mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha_{2})$ . Then by the discussion in Construction 2.45 line bundles with connection $(\mathcal{O}_{U},d+\alpha_{1})$ and $(\mathcal{O}_{U},d+\alpha_{2})$ are locally isomorphic, which means1414 14 Indeed, if $(\mathcal{O}_{U},\nabla)$ and $(\mathcal{O}_{U},\nabla^{\prime})$ are isomorphic, the isomorphism is given by multiplication by $f$ and then $\nabla^{\prime}=\nabla+d\log f$ . that (after some cover) $\alpha_{1}=\alpha_{2}+d\log f$ for some function $f$ . ∎

### 2.8. Restricted Poisson structures

We recall and try to motivate the definition of restricted Poisson structure due to [BK].

Recall that a Poisson bracket on a commutative ring $A$ is a Lie bracket $\{-,-\}$ on $A$ that is also a derivation in each variable. If the corresponding derivations are $B$ -linear for some algebra $B$ with a homomorphism $B\rightarrow A$ then we will say that the Poisson bracket is over $B$ (or $B$ -linear).

#### Construction 2.47 (Free Poisson algebra).

Let $V$ be a $B$ -module. Let $T(V)$ be the tensor algebra over $B$ and $L(V)$ the free Lie algebra over $B$ on $V$ correspondingly. Then $T(V)$ is the universal envelopping algebra of $L(V)$ . Viewed this way, $T(V)$ acquires a PBW-filtration $F_{*}^{PBW}T(V)$ , for which $\gr_{*}^{PBW}T(V)\simeq\Sym^{*}_{B}V$ . One can also consider the corresponding Rees algebra1515 15 In [BK] $Q(V)$ is called the algebra of quantized polynomials in $V$ , hence the notation. $Q(V)\coloneqq\oplus_{i}F_{i}^{PBW}T(V)\cdot h^{i}$ corresponding to $F_{*}^{PBW}T(V)$ ; this is an $h$ -torsion free $B[h]$ -algebra such that $Q(V)[h^{-1}]\simeq T(V)[h,h^{-1}]$ and $Q(V)/h\simeq\gr_{*}^{PBW}T(V)$ . Since $[F_{i}^{PBW}T(V),F_{j}^{PBW}T(V)]\subset F_{i+j-1}^{PBW}T(V)$ one has $[Q(V),Q(V)]\subset h\cdot Q(V)$ and there is a natural Poisson bracket on $\gr_{*}^{PBW}T(V)$ defined by

$$ h\cdot\{f,g\}\coloneqq[\tilde{f},\tilde{g}]\mod h^{2} $$

where $\tilde{f}$ and $\tilde{g}$ are some lifts of $f,g\in\gr_{*}^{PBW}T(V)\simeq Q(V)/h$ to $Q(V)$ .

The resulting Poisson bracket on $\gr_{*}^{PBW}T(V)\simeq\Sym^{*}_{B}L(V)$ is identified with the Kostant-Kirillov bracket, namely the unique bracket that on linear functions $z,w\in L(v)\subset\Sym^{*}_{B}L(V)$ is given by $\{z,w\}\coloneqq[z,w]\in L(V)$ . We call $\Sym^{*}_{B}L(V)$ with the above bracket the free Poisson algebra on $V$ and denote it $\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ .

This is justified by the universal property: namely, any $B$ -linear map $f\colon V\rightarrow A$ to a Poisson algebra $A$ extends to a Poisson algebra homomorphism $\mathrm{Pois}(V)\rightarrow A$ . Indeed, $f$ extends to a Lie algebra map $f^{\prime}\colon L(V)\rightarrow A$ with respect to the Poisson bracket on $A$ , and then we can extend $f^{\prime}$ to an algebra map $\Sym^{*}_{B}L(V)\rightarrow A$ . Since the Poisson bracket on $\Sym^{*}_{B}L(V)$ is uniquely defined by its restriction to $L(V)$ we get that this map is automatically Poisson. In particular, for any Poisson algebra $A$ there is a natural Poisson algebra map $\mathrm{Pois}(A)\rightarrow A$ .

#### Remark 2.48.

The construction $V\mapsto\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ defines a monad on $B$ -modules. Indeed, we have a natural map $V\rightarrow\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ and a natural map $\mathrm{Pois}(\mathrm{Pois}(V))\rightarrow\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ induced by the Poisson structure on $\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ that endow $\mathrm{Pois}(-)$ with a structure of a monad. Then, using the morphism $\mathrm{Pois}(A)\rightarrow A$ one can define Poisson $B$ -algebras simply as modules over $\mathrm{Pois}(-)$ .

The idea of a restricted Poisson structure on $A$ is that together with a Poisson bracket one should include a restricted $p$ -power operation $-^{[p]}\colon A\rightarrow A$ that would turn $(A,\{-,-\})$ in a restricted Lie algebra. However, the natural question is how $-^{[p]}$ should interact with the mulptiplication on $A$ . This is what we will try to explain in the rest of this section. First, motivated by Construction 2.47 we can build the free restricted Poisson algebra:

#### Construction 2.49 (Free restricted Poisson algebra: part I).

Let $V$ be a $B$ -module and consider the free restricted Lie algebra $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ on $V$ . The underlying $B$ -module of $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ has a natural filtration $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)^{\leq*}$ with $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)^{\leq-1}=0$ , $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)^{\leq 0}\simeq L(V)$ , and $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)^{\leq i+1}$ is inductively defined as $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)^{\leq i}+(L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)^{\leq i})^{[p]}$ , where by the Jacobson’s formula the latter expression is a well-defined $B$ -module. One has $\gr_{*}(L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))\simeq\oplus_{i\geq 0}L(V)^{(i)}$ , where $L(V)^{(i)}\coloneqq L(V)\otimes_{B,F_{B}^{i}}B$ is the $i$ ’th Frobenius twist.

We can consider the corresponding universal enveloping algebra and its Rees algebra $Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\coloneqq\oplus_{i}F_{i}^{PBW}U(L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ with respect to the PBW-filtration. One can then define the free restricted Poisson algebra $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ as $Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h\simeq\Sym L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ . As in Construction 2.47 this is naturally a Poisson algebra via the Lie bracket on $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ . However, we also need to endow $\Sym L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ with a natural restricted structure. For this we need a little more preparation.

Let $L$ be a restricted Lie algebra over $B$ (e.g. $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ ), and consider its universal enveloping algebra $U(L)$ . Let us denote by $U_{h}(L)\coloneqq\oplus_{n}F_{n}^{PBW}U(L)\cdot h^{n}$ its Rees algebra with respect to the PBW-filtration. $L$ embeds in $U_{h}(L)$ as $h\cdot L\subset h\cdot F_{1}^{PBW}U(L)\subset U_{h}(L)$ and generates $U_{h}(L)$ over $B[h]$ .

Consider the map $\theta\colon L\rightarrow U_{h}(L)$ which sends $x\in L$ to $x^{p}-h^{p-1}x^{[p]}$ . Note that it is $F_{B}$ -linear.

#### Lemma 2.50.

$\theta$ is additive and its image lands in the center $Z(U_{h}(L))\subset U_{h}(L)$ .

#### Proof.

We will denote by $[-,-]_{L}$ the Lie bracket in $L$ to distinguish it from the one in $U_{h}(L)$ . The additivity follows from the Jacobson’s formula (see Lemma 2.13 and part(2) of Definition 2.16). For the statement about the center, it is enough to show that $[\theta(x),y]=0$ for $y\in L$ . Note that for $x,y\in L$ we have $[x,y]=h\cdot[x,y]_{L}$ . Thus for $y\in L$ we have $[x^{p},y]=\ad(x)^{p}(y)=h^{p}\ad_{L}(x)^{p}(y)$ . On the other hand, $[x^{[p]},y]=h\ad_{L}(x)^{p}(y)$ . This shows that $[\theta(x),y]=0$ . ∎

The map from 2.50 gives a map of $B$ -algebras

$$ \theta\colon\Sym L^{(1)}\rightarrow Z(U_{h}(L)). $$

Let $-^{(1)}\colon L\rightarrow L^{(1)}$ be the natural map sending $x$ to $x\otimes 1$ . Consider also the map $p\colon Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\twoheadrightarrow\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\simeq Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h$ given by reduction modulo $h$ . Note that given $x\in\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ and any lift $\widetilde{x}\in Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ the element $(\widetilde{x})^{p}\in Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ is well-defined modulo $h^{p}$ . Indeed, by Jacobson’s formula

$$ (\widetilde{x}+hy)^{p}=\widetilde{x}^{p}+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}{L_{i}}(\widetilde{x},hy)\pmod{h^{p}}, $$

but each ${L_{i}}(\widetilde{x},hy)$ is Lie polynomial of total Lie degree1616 16 Meaning that it is expressed as a sum of terms each involving a composition of $p-1$ commutators. $p-1$ and (see the explicit description of $L_{i}$ in Lemma 2.13) $L_{i}(\widetilde{x},hy)=h^{i}L_{i}(\widetilde{x},{y})$ . Thus $(\widetilde{x}+hy)^{p}=\widetilde{x}^{p}\mod{h^{p}}.$

Then one can reconstruct the restricted structure on $L$ in terms of $\theta$ , namely

$$ h^{p-1}x^{[p]}=\tilde{x}^{p}-\theta(x^{(1)})\pmod{h^{p}}. $$

Under the identification $h^{p-1}Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h^{p}\simeq Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h$ this defines $x^{[p]}$ uniquely. The idea now is to define the restricted structure on the whole of $\Sym L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ in a similar manner using the map $\theta$ .

#### Lemma 2.51.

- (1) For any $x\in\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ and any lift $\widetilde{x}\in Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ the element $\widetilde{x}^{p}-\theta(x^{(1)})$ is divisible by $h^{p-1}$ .

- (2) The map $-^{[p]}\colon\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\rightarrow\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ defined by

$$ h^{p-1}x^{[p]}=\tilde{x}^{p}-\theta(x^{(1)})\pmod{h^{p}} $$

endows $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\simeq\Sym L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ with a restricted Lie algebra structure that agrees with the one on $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ .

#### Proof.

Consider the $B[h]/h^{p-1}$ -algebra given by $Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h^{p-1}$ . By the discussion above concerning the Jacobson’s formula, $x\mapsto\tilde{x}^{p}$ produces a well-defined map $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\simeq Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h\rightarrow Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)/h^{p-1}$ . By [BK, Lemma 1.3] this is in fact an algebra homomorphism. Moreover, it agrees with $\theta$ on $L_{\mathsf{rest}}$ and since $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\coloneqq\Sym L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ it agrees with $\theta$ on the whole $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ . We get that $\widetilde{x}^{p}-\theta(x^{(1)})=0$ modulo $h^{p-1}$ for any $x\in\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ .

For (2) we need to check the defining properties of restricted Lie algebra (Definition 2.16). First of all, $-^{[p]}$ is Frobenius-linear since $x\rightarrow\tilde{x}^{p}$ and $\theta$ are. Note that since $\{x,y\}=h[\tilde{x},\tilde{y}]\mod h^{2}$ one has

$$ \ad_{[-,-]}(\tilde{x}^{p})(\tilde{y})=\ad_{[-,-]}(\tilde{x})^{p}(\tilde{y})=h^{p}\cdot\ad_{\{-,-\}}(x)^{p}(y)\mod h^{p+1}. $$

Since $\theta(x^{(1)})$ is central applying $[-,\tilde{y}]$ to the expression for $x^{[p]}$ we get that

$$ h^{p}\ad_{\{-,-\}}(x^{[p]})(y)=h^{p}\ad_{\{-,-\}}(x)^{p}(y)\mod h^{p+1}. $$

Finally, the formula for $(x+y)^{[p]}$ follows from the Jacobson formula. Namely, $\theta$ is a homomorphism, so we have $\theta(x^{(1)}+y^{(1)})=\theta(x^{(1)})+\theta(y^{(1)})$ , and

$$ h^{p-1}\cdot((x+y)^{[p]}-x^{[p]}-y^{[p]})=(\tilde{x}+\tilde{y})^{p}-\tilde{x}^{p}-\tilde{y}^{p}\mod h^{p} $$

where the right hand side is given by $h^{p-1}\sum_{i}L_{i}(x,y)$ (2.13, here since each $L_{i}$ is a Lie polynomial of degree $p-1$ we have $L_{i}(\tilde{x},\tilde{y})=h^{p-1}L_{i}(x,y)$ ). ∎

#### Construction 2.52 (Free restricted Poisson algebra: part II).

Continuing Construction 2.49, via Lemma 2.51 we can now endow $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ not only with a Poisson bracket, but also a $p$ -power operation $-^{[p]}$ such that $(\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V),\{-,-\},-^{[p]})$ becomes a restricted Lie algebra. This allows to consider $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ and a homomorphism of algebras

$$ \mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))\rightarrow\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V) $$

defined (via the identification $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))\simeq\Sym L_{\mathsf{rest}}(\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ ) by sending $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ to $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ using the structure of restricted Lie algebra, and then extending by multiplicativity. We also have an embedding $V\subset L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\subset\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ which with the map above endows $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}$ with a structure of a monad on the category of $B$ -modules.

#### Definition 2.53 (Restricted Poisson algebra).

A restricted Poisson algebra $A$ over $B$ is a module over the monad given by $V\mapsto\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ .

#### Remark 2.54.

We note that there are a lot of structures underlying the restricted Poisson structure. Let $A$ be a restricted Poisson $B$ -algebra.

- • There is a natural map of monads $\mathrm{Pois}(-)\rightarrow\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(-)$ induced by the embedding $\Sym^{*}(L(V))\rightarrow\Sym^{*}(L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ , which in turn is induced by $L(V)\rightarrow L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ for each $B$ -module $V$ . Thus by Remark 2.48, $A$ has a natural Poisson algebra structure.

- • There is a natural map of monads $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\rightarrow\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(-)$ induced by the embedding $L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\rightarrow\Sym^{*}(L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ for each $B$ -module $V$ . This gives a restricted Lie algebra structure on $A$ .

- • There is a natural diagram of monads $\textstyle{L(-)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\textstyle{\mathrm{Pois}(-)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\textstyle{L_{\mathsf{rest}}(-)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\textstyle{\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(-)}$ given by the above maps and embeddings $L(V)\rightarrow\Sym^{*}(L(V))$ and $L(V)\rightarrow L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ for each $B$ -module $V$ correspondingly, which shows that the Lie algebra structure on $A$ given by the above Poisson structure and restricted Lie structure on $A$ agree.

Finally, let us describe more explicitly how $(-)^{[p]}$ in $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ interects with multiplication.

#### Construction 2.55 (Polynomial $P(x,y)$ and formula for $(xy)^{[p]}$ .).

Consider $V\simeq Bx\oplus By$ a free $B$ -module of rank 2 with basis given by $x$ and $y$ . Consider the (non-restricted) algebras $Q(V)$ and $\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ . Then by [BK, Equation 1.3] (which in turn follows from [BK, Lemma 1.3]) the expression $(xy)^{p}-x^{p}y^{p}$ is divisible by $h^{p-1}$ . One can the define a Poisson polynomial $P(x,y)\in\mathrm{Pois}(x,y)\coloneqq\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ by

$$ h^{p-1}P(x,y)=(xy)^{p}-x^{p}y^{p}\pmod{h^{p}Q(V)}. $$

Then, for the restricted structures in $Q_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ we have an equality

$$ \displaystyle h^{p-1}(xy)^{[p]}\coloneqq(xy)^{p} \displaystyle-\theta(xy)=x^{p}y^{p}+h^{p-1}P(x,y)-(x^{p}-h^{p-1}x^{[p]})(y^{p}-h^{p-1}y^{[p]})= \displaystyle=h^{p-1}(x^{p}y^{[p]}+x^{[p]}y+P(x,y))\pmod{h^{p}}, $$

which shows that $(xy)^{[p]}=x^{p}y^{[p]}+x^{[p]}y+P(x,y)\in\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)$ . Note that for any $V$ this formula uniquely defines the restricted structure on $\mathrm{Pois}_{\mathsf{rest}}(V)\simeq\Sym^{*}(L_{\mathsf{rest}}(V))$ by induction on the degree.

This way for any restricted Poisson algebra $A$ and any two elements $x,y\in A$ we have

$$ (xy)^{[p]}=x^{p}y^{[p]}+x^{[p]}y+P(x,y), $$

where the value of $P(x,y)\in A$ is computed via the map $\mathrm{Pois}(A)\rightarrow A$ . In fact, since the above formula defines the restricted structure on a free restricted Poisson algebra uniquely, one can give an alternative definition of a restricted Poisson algebra as a Poisson $B$ -algebra $A$ with a restricted $p$ -power operation $-^{[p]}$ such that $(A,\{-,-\},-^{[p]})$ is restricted Lie algebra and that the relation (2.5) is satisfied for any $x,y\in A$ . This is how it is defined in [BK] (namely, see [BK, Definiton 1.8]).

Equation 2.5 is hard to check in practice in the original form essentially because the definition of $P(x,y)$ is complicated (and not very explicit). But, at least when $p>2$ there is an equivalent condition that is easier to check:

#### Remark 2.56.

Let $p>2$ . Let $x\in\mathrm{Pois}(V)$ be some element. Then, for any lift $\widetilde{x}\in Q(V)$ we have $(\widetilde{x}^{2})^{p}=\widetilde{x}^{p}\cdot\widetilde{x}^{p}$ and so $P(x,x)=0$ . From this and (2.5) we get that

$$ (x^{2})^{[p]}=2x^{[p]}x^{p}. $$

Note that $xy=\frac{1}{4}((x+y)^{2}-(x-y)^{2})$ . Thus, applying the restricted power, we get

$$ (xy)^{[p]}=\tfrac{1}{4}((x+y)^{2}-(x-y)^{2})^{[p]} $$

which, using Jacobson’s formula, gives an expression for $P(x,y)$ in terms of $-^{[p]}$ applied to squares and some Poisson polynomial in $x$ , $y$ , $x^{[p]}$ and $y^{[p]}$ . This shows that checking Equation (2.5) reduces to checking that $-^{[p]}$ together with the Poisson bracket give a restricted structure in the Lie algebra structure and that Equation (2.5) holds for all $x$ .

In particular, $(A,\{-,-\},-^{[p]})$ defines a restricted Poisson algebra 2.5 if and only if

- • $(A,\{-,-\})$ is a Poisson algebra;

- • $(A,\{-,-\},-^{[p]})$ defines a restricted Lie algebra;

- • $(x^{2})^{[p]}=2x^{[p]}x^{p}$ for any $x\in A$ .

This simplification of [BK, Definiton 1.8] was also previously observed in [BYZ].

### 2.9. Restricted symplectic geometry

#### Definition 2.57.

A symplectic scheme $(X,\omega)$ over $S$ is a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme $X$ with a non-degenerate globally defined closed 2-form $\omega\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{2}_{X})$ .

Since $\omega$ is non-degenerate it induces an identification $\mathcal{T}_{X}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega^{1}_{X}$ via $\xi\mapsto\iota_{\xi}\omega$ , where $\iota_{\xi}$ is the contraction with $\xi$ . This way $\omega$ also defines a section $\omega^{-1}$ of $\wedge^{2}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{T}_{X}$ , which then gives a Poisson bracket on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ : $\{f,g\}\coloneqq\langle\omega^{-1},df\wedge dg\rangle$ . The property that $d\omega=0$ translates to the Jacobi identity for $\{-,-\}$ : in particular $(\mathcal{O}_{X},\{-,-\})$ defines a sheaf of Lie algebras over $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ .

Having a Poisson bracket $\{-,-\}$ , for any $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ the bracket $\{f,-\}$ defines a derivation $H_{f}\colon\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}$ . This gives a map of sheaves $H_{-}\colon\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{T}_{X}$ locally sending $f\mapsto H_{f}$ .

The following definition is classical:

#### Definition 2.58.

A derivation $\xi\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1})$ is called Hamiltonian if $\xi=H_{f}$ for some $f\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X})$ .

#### Remark 2.59.

Tracing through the definitions one can see that the equation $\xi=H_{f}$ is in fact equivalent to $\iota_{\xi}\omega=df$ . Since $\omega$ is non-degenerate one sees from this that Hamiltonian vector fields locally generate $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ over $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ .

One of the main ideas in [BK] is that in char $p$ there is a natural enhancement of the usual Poisson structure called restricted Poisson structure (see Definition 2.53). Namely, together with the Poisson bracket $\{-,-\}$ on $X$ they ask for a restricted $p$ -th power operation $-^{[p]}\colon\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}$ that turns $(\mathcal{O}_{X},\{-,-\})$ into a restricted Lie algebra compatibly with such structure on $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ (meaning that $H_{f^{[p]}}=H_{f}^{[p]}$ ). It should also interact with multiplication in a particular way, namely for any $f,g\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ we should have

$$ (fg)^{[p]}=f^{p}g^{[p]}+f^{[p]}g^{p}+P(f,g), $$

where $P(x,y)$ is a certain Poisson polynomial (see Remark 2.55). By Remark 2.56, if $p>2$ , this is also equivalent to the simpler relation

$$ (f^{2})^{[p]}=2f^{[p]}f^{p} $$

for any $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X}$ .

In [BK, Theorem 1.11] Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin show that given a symplectic $S$ -scheme $(X,\omega)$ Hamiltonian vector fields are closed under the restricted $p$ -th power $-^{[p]}$ if and only if1717 17 Here $C\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{2}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{2,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ is the Cartier operator and the condition $C(\omega)=0$ is equivalent to $\omega$ being exact locally in Zariski topology. $C(\omega)=0$ . Under this assumption, a consequence of [BK, Theorem 1.12] is that restricted structures extending the Poisson bracket given by $\omega$ are in bijection with classes $[\eta]\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X}/d(\mathcal{O}_{X}))$ such that $d[\eta]=\omega$ . Note that such classes $\eta$ form a torsor on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ over the vector bundle $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}/d(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X})\simeq\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ .

#### Definition 2.60.

A restricted symplectic $S$ -scheme $(X,[\eta])$ is a pair of a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme $X$ and a section $[\eta]\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X}/d(\mathcal{O}_{X}))$ such that $\omega\coloneqq d\eta\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{2}_{X})$ is non-degenerate.

#### Remark 2.61.

Given $[\eta]$ , one reconstructs the restricted structure $-^{[p]}$ via an explicit formula $f^{[p]}=H_{f}^{p-1}(\langle H_{f},\eta\rangle)-\langle H_{f}^{[p]},\eta\rangle$ . Also, any two restricted structures $-^{[p]_{1}},-^{[p]_{2}}$ differ by a Frobenius-differentiation of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ : this can be seen directly from Equation 2.7.

The following remark will be important.

#### Remark 2.62 (Doing differential geometry on $X$ as a scheme over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and $S$ is the same).

Let $X$ be an $S$ -scheme and let $X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ be the reduced Frobenius. Then we claim that providing $X$ with the structure of a restricted symplectic scheme over $S$ is the samle as providing it with the same structure over the reduced twist $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Indeed, first of all we have a commutative diagram

$$ \textstyle{X\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{S} $$

which gives an exact sequence

$$ F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\Omega^{1}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\xrightarrow{F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}}\Omega^{1}_{X}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X/X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow 0. $$

Since the pull-back map $F_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\Omega^{1}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X}$ is 0 we get that $\Omega^{1}_{X/X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq\Omega^{1}_{X}$ and so $X$ is pseudo-smooth over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . We also have isomorphisms $\Omega^{i}_{X/X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq\Omega^{i}_{X}$ and, more generally of the de Rham complex $\mathrm{dR}_{X/X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ . Lastly, essentially by the definition of reduced twist, $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ for $X$ considered as an $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -scheme and as $S$ -scheme coincide (because $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is defined as the image of relative Frobenius). Thus symplectic and, more generally, restricted symplectic structures on $X$ as an $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -scheme or an $S$ -scheme are the same thing.

### 2.10. The group scheme $G_{0}$ and Darboux lemma

Another insight of Bezrukavnikov and Kaledin is that restricted Poisson structures on $X$ can be interpreted in terms of “formal geometry” and related torsors. To recall it let us introduce one more piece of notation.

#### Construction 2.63 (Algebra $A_{0}$ ).

Fix a number $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $S=\Spec\mathbb{F}_{p}$ . Let $V$ be a vector space scheme of dimension $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ (so $V\simeq\Spec\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{1},\ldots,x_{d}]$ ) and let $W=V\oplus V^{\vee}$ be the total space of the cotangent bundle to $V$ : thus $W$ is a symplectic vector space of dimension $2d$ . Let $y_{i}$ be the dual coordinates to $x_{i}$ ; one has $W\simeq\Spec\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{1},\ldots,x_{d},y_{1},\ldots,y_{d}]$ .

Consider the ring of functions on the Frobenius neighborhood $F_{W}^{-1}(\{0\})$ of $0$ in $W$ (see Example 2.11). Explicitly, put1818 18 This algebra is denoted $A$ in [BK, Section 3].

$$ A_{0}\coloneqq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{i},y_{j}]_{1\leq i,j\leq d}/x_{i}^{p}=y_{j}^{p}=0. $$

One has $\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}}\simeq(\oplus_{i=1}^{d}A_{0}\cdot dx_{i})\oplus(\oplus_{i=1}^{d}A_{0}\cdot dy_{i})$ (namely, since $dx_{i}^{p}=dy_{j}^{p}=0$ the map $\Omega^{1}_{W}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{i},y_{j}]}A_{0}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}}$ is an isomorphism). In particular, $A_{0}$ is pseudo-smooth over $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ . $\Spec A_{0}$ endowed with a natural restricted symplectic structure given by the 1-form

$$ \eta_{\mathsf{can}}=\sum_{i=1}^{d}y_{i}dx_{i}\in\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}}. $$

Indeed, the 2-form $\omega\coloneqq d\eta_{\mathsf{can}}=\sum_{i}dy_{i}\wedge dx_{i}\in\Omega^{2}_{A_{0}}$ is easily seen to be non-degenerate.

Similarly, for any $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra $R$ we can consider an $R$ -algebra

$$ A_{0}(R)\coloneqq A_{0}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}R. $$

We have $\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)/R}\simeq\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}R$ and via this identification the pair $(\Spec A_{0}(R),[\eta_{\mathsf{can}}\otimes 1])$ defines a restricted symplectic $R$ -scheme (see Definition 2.60). Further we will denote $\eta_{\mathsf{can}}\otimes 1$ by $\eta_{\mathsf{can}}$ for convenience.

#### Construction 2.64 (Group scheme $G_{0}$ ).

Consider the functor

$$ A_{0}\colon R\mapsto A_{0}(R) $$

on $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebras. Let $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ be the functor

$$ \underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})\colon R\mapsto\mathrm{Aut}_{R}(A_{0}(R))\simeq\mathrm{Iso}_{R}(\Spec A_{0}(R),\Spec A_{0}(R)) $$

that sends an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra $R$ to the group of $R$ -linear algebra automorphisms. Since $A_{0}(R)$ is a free module over $R$ one sees that $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ with represented by the affine group subscheme of $\GL(A_{0})$ given by those linear automorphisms that preserve multiplication on $A_{0}$ . Finally, let $G_{0}\subset\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ be the functor

$$ R\mapsto\mathrm{Aut}_{R}^{\mathsf{rest}}((\Spec A_{0}(R),[\eta_{\mathsf{can}}])) $$

that sends $R$ to the group of $R$ -algebra automorphisms of $A_{0}(R)$ that preserve the restricted symplectic structure given by $\eta_{\mathsf{can}}$ . It can be seen to be represented by a group subscheme of $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ : namely, one adds equations to $\phi\in\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ saying that $\mathsf{C}(\phi^{*}\eta_{\mathsf{can}}-\eta_{\mathsf{can}})=0$ (which is equivalent to $[\eta_{\mathsf{can}}]\in\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}/d(A_{0}(R))$ being preserved under $\phi$ ).

#### Remark 2.65.

The group scheme $H\coloneqq\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ is not particularly nice, for example it is not reduced. Indeed, let $I_{0}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{d},y_{1},\ldots,y_{d})\subset A_{0}$ be the maximal ideal. Note that for a reduced $R$ any $\phi\in\mathrm{Aut}_{R}(A_{0}(R))$ preserves $I_{0}(R)\coloneqq I_{0}\otimes R$ : indeed $I_{0}(R)$ in this case coincides with nilradical of $A_{0}(R)$ . If $H$ were reduced this would also be true for the $\mathcal{O}(H)$ -point of $H$ given by the identity map $H\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}H$ . Since any $R$ -point of $H$ factors through this one we would get that any $\phi\in\mathrm{Aut}_{R}(A_{0}(R))$ even for non-reduced $R$ also preserve $I_{0}(R)$ . However, this is not true: whenever $\alpha_{p}(R)\neq 0$ one can consider an automorphism sending $x_{i}$ to $x_{i}+\varepsilon$ for some non-zero $\varepsilon\in\alpha_{p}(R)$ : this gives a well defined automorphism of $A_{0}(R)$ that doesn’t preserve $I_{0}(R)$ . Similarly, one sees that $G_{0}$ is also not reduced: namely $\eta_{\mathsf{can}}$ is also preserved by the above automorphism.

#### Construction 2.66 (Torsor of “Frobenius-frames”).

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth scheme over a base scheme $S$ such that $\rk H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X/S})=2d$ . Consider the algebra $A_{0}$ from Construction 2.63 for that particular $d$ . Consider the reduced Frobenius map $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (Construction 2.10).

One can construct a canonical $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ -torsor $\mathcal{M}_{X}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ as follows. Namely, for a map $T\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ one puts

$$ \mathcal{M}_{X}(T)\coloneqq\mathrm{Iso}_{T}(\Spec A_{0}\times T,X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}T) $$

This is a sheaf in flat topology on the category of schemes over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Note that $\mathcal{M}_{X}$ has a natural action of $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ . Moreover, flat locally on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ one has an isomorphism

$$ {\mathcal{M}_{X}|}_{U}\simeq\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})\times U. $$

Indeed, let $U\rightarrow X$ be a Zariski cover that trivializes $\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ . Then $U$ is still pseudo-smooth, so $F_{U}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon U\rightarrow U^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is faithfully flat (as well as the composite map $U\rightarrow U^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ ) and by Lemma 2.67 below

$$ X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}U\simeq U\times_{U^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}U\simeq\Spec A_{0}\times U. $$

This way the restriction ${\mathcal{M}_{X}|}_{U}$ is identified with the functor

$$ (T\rightarrow U)\mapsto\mathrm{Iso}_{T}(\Spec A_{0}\times T,\Spec A_{0}\times T) $$

which is exactly $X\times\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ . This way we see that the action of $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ on $\mathcal{M}_{X}$ is effective and that the latter indeed defines an $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ -torsor over $X^{\prime}$ (in flat topology). In [BK] it is called the torsor of Frobenius frames on $X$ .

#### Lemma 2.67.

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth scheme over a base scheme $S$ . Then Zariski locally on $X$ one has a natural isomorphism

$$ X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}X\simeq X\times\Spec A_{0}. $$

#### Proof.

When $X$ is smooth over $S$ , $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is given by the relative Frobenius $F_{X/S}\colon X\rightarrow X^{(1)}$ and the statement is classical: Zariski locally one has an étale map $X\rightarrow\mathbb{A}^{2d}_{S}$ and in the case of affine space the isomorphism is easy to construct explicitly.

For general pseudo-smooth scheme we use Proposition 2.35: namely, $X$ Zariski locally is identified with the Frobenius neighborhood $(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)$ in a smooth $S$ -scheme $Y$ of a closed subscheme $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Following Remark 2.33 the reduced Frobenius map $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq Z$ is the pull-back of $F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon Y\rightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . This way we have

$$ X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}X\simeq(Y\times_{Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}Y)\times_{Y}Z $$

and we reduce to the smooth case. ∎

#### Construction 2.68 (Restricted symplectic structures as reductions of $\mathcal{M}_{X}$ to $G_{0}$ ).

Another observation of [BK] is that restricted Poisson structures on $X$ can be seen as reductions of the canonical $\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ -torsor $\mathcal{M}_{X}$ to the subgroup $G_{0}\subset\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})$ .

Let us remind this identification. By Remark 2.62 given a restricted symplectic $S$ -scheme $(X,[\eta])$ one can equally consider it as a restricted symplectic scheme over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Then one can define a functor $\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}$ on schemes over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ as follows. First note that for any $T$ one gets a restricted sympectic $T$ -scheme $(\Spec A_{0},[\eta_{\mathsf{can}}])\times T$ . Second, given a map $T\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ one can take $(X,[\eta])\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}T$ which also gives a restricted symplectic $T$ -scheme. Then one defines

$$ (T\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\mapsto\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}(T)\coloneqq\mathrm{Iso}_{T}^{\mathsf{rest}}((\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})\times T,(X,[\eta])\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}T) $$

where $\mathrm{Iso}_{T}^{\mathsf{rest}}$ denotes isomorphisms over $T$ that preserve the restricted symplectic structure. This is a sheaf in flat toplogy on the category of schemes over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ with a natural action of $G_{0}$ . Moreover, picking a map $U\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ as in Construction 2.66 such that $U$ is affine we get that $(X,[\eta])\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}U$ is in fact isomorphic to $(\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})\times U$ and so the restriction ${\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}|}_{U}$ can be identified with the functor

$$ (T\rightarrow U)\mapsto\mathrm{Iso}_{T}^{\mathsf{rest}}((\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})\times T,(\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})\times T) $$

or, in other words,

$$ {\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}|}_{U}\simeq G_{0}\times U. $$

This way $\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}$ defines a $G_{0}$ -torsor on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and by construction one has a natural isomorphism

$$ \alpha\colon\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}\times^{G_{0}}\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})\simeq\mathcal{M}_{X}. $$

The other way around, having a $G_{0}$ -torsor $\mathcal{M}^{\prime}$ over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ such that

$$ \mathcal{M}^{\prime}\times^{G_{0}}\underline{\mathrm{Aut}}(A_{0})\simeq\mathcal{M}_{X} $$

we can take a cover $U\rightarrow X$ as above such that $X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}U\simeq\Spec A_{0}\times U$ and descend the restricted symplectic $U$ -scheme given by $(\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})\times U$ to $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ using the descent data provided by $\mathcal{M}^{\prime}$ and $\alpha$ .

#### Remark 2.69.

Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra. Then one can show that any two restricted Poisson structures over $R$ on $\Spec A_{0}(R)$ are isomorphic (see [BK, Proposition 3.4]).

Finally, let us fix some terminology:

#### Definition 2.70.

The $G_{0}$ -torsor $\mathcal{M}_{X,[\eta]}$ over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is called the torsor of Darboux frames associated to $(X,[\eta])$ .

#### Remark 2.71.

The fact that there exists a faithfully flat cover $U\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ such that $X\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}U\simeq(\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})\times U$ as restricted Poisson schemes, can be considered as an analogue of the Darboux lemma in the restricted symplectic setting. Indeed, we see that $(\Spec A_{0},\eta_{\mathsf{can}})$ serves as a “local model” for any restricted symplectic structure.

## 3. Sheaves of algebras $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\flat}$ and their categories of modules

For the rest of this section let $\mathbb{S}=\mathbb{P}^{1}$ do we want base to be k or anything?. For each dimension $n$ we will define two sheaves of algebras on $\mathbb{S}$ : the compactified version $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ of the (Rees construction of) reduced Weyl algebra on $2n$ generators and a certain auxhillary algebra $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\flat}$ which is obtained as another central reduction from Weyl algebra on $4n$ -generators. The goal later will be to construct a certain canonical action of $G_{0}$ on the category $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}-\Mod$ . For now, following [BV] we will construct an action of $G_{0}$ on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\flat}-\Mod$ : it then will be crucially used to construct the desired action on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}-\Mod$ .

### 3.1. Rees construction over $\mathbb{S}\coloneqq\mathbb{P}^{1}$

Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a quasicoherent sheaf of associative (but not necessarily commutative) algebras over a base scheme $Y$ . Let $\mathcal{B}_{\leq*}=\ldots\subset\mathcal{B}_{\leq n}\subset\mathcal{B}_{\leq n+1}\subset\ldots$ be an increasing filtration on $\mathcal{B}$ indexed by integers. We assume that the filtration is multiplicative ( $\mathcal{B}_{\leq i}\cdot\mathcal{B}_{\leq j}\subset\mathcal{B}_{\leq i+j}$ ) and exhaustive (namely $\mathcal{B}=\text{colim}_{n}\mathcal{B}_{\leq n}$ ).

The idea of our construction is very simple: namely we glue up the Rees construction of $\mathcal{B}_{\leq*}$ (considered as a sheaf on $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}$ ) with the constant sheaf given by $\mathcal{B}$ on $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ along their common intersection. First let us remind the usual Rees construction and its properties.

#### Construction 3.1 (Rees construction over $\mathbb{A}^{1}$ ).

Let $h$ be a formal variable. Let $\mathcal{B}_{\leq*}$ be as above.

Define the Rees construction $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ of the filtered algebra $\mathcal{B}_{\leq*}$ as a subsheaf of algebras

$$ \mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}\coloneqq\oplus_{i}\mathcal{B}_{\leq i}\cdot h^{i}\subset\mathcal{B}[h,h^{-1}]\coloneqq\mathcal{B}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Z}[h,h^{-1}]. $$

Since $\mathcal{B}_{\leq i}\cdot\mathcal{B}_{\leq j}\subset\mathcal{B}_{\leq i+j}$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\leq i}\subset\mathcal{B}_{\leq i+1}$ , the multiplication on $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ is well-defined and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ defines a (quasicoherent) subsheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ -algebras in $\mathcal{B}[h,h^{-1}]$ . One also has isomorphisms

$$ \mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}/h\simeq\gr_{*}\mathcal{B}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}[h^{-1}]\simeq\mathcal{B}[h,h^{-1}]. $$

Here for the second isomorphism we used the exhaustiveness of filtration.

Using a monoidal equivalence of categories of quasicoherent $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ -modules and quasicoherent sheaves on $\mathbb{A}^{1}\times Y$ we can view the $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ -algebra $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ as a quasicoherent sheaf of algebras $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ over $\mathbb{A}^{1}\times Y$ . Formulas 3.1 then give

$$ {{\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}|}_{\{0\}\times Y}}\simeq\gr_{*}\mathcal{B}\quad\text{and}\quad{\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}|}_{\mathbb{G}_{m}\times Y}\simeq p_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}^{*}\mathcal{B} $$

where $p_{\mathbb{G}_{m}}\colon\mathbb{G}_{m}\times Y\rightarrow Y$ is the projection.

#### Construction 3.2 (A variant over the center).

Let $Z(\mathcal{B})\subset\mathcal{B}$ be the center and define the filtration $Z(\mathcal{B})_{\leq*}\coloneqq Z(\mathcal{B})\cap\mathcal{B}_{\leq*}$ . This filtration is also multiplicative and exhaustive and we can consider the corresponding Rees construction $Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ . Then $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ is naturally a sheaf of algebras over $Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ and as such also defines a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras over the relative spectrum $\Spec_{\mathbb{A}^{1}\times Y}(Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}})$ .

#### Construction 3.3 (Descent to $[\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]$ ).

Consider the standard action of $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ on $\mathbb{A}^{1}$ (such that $t\circ h=th$ for $t\in\mathbb{G}_{m}$ ). It induces a $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action on $Y\times\mathbb{A}^{1}$ (where the action on $Y$ is trivial) and endows $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ with a $\mathbb{Z}$ -grading such that $\mathcal{O}_{Y}$ has grading 0 and the variable $h$ has grading 1. One can consider the corresponding quotient stack $[\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y$ . Using faithfully flat descent the abelian category of quasicoherent sheaves on $[\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y$ can be identified with the category of quasicoherent sheaves of graded $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ -modules on $Y$ .

The algebra $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ comes with a natural grading $(\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}})^{i}\coloneqq\mathcal{B}_{\leq i}\cdot h^{i}$ that makes it into a graded $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ -algebra. This way we can also descend $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ to a quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{B}_{[\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}$ of algebras on $[\mathbb{A}^{1}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y$ .

The descent above also has a variant over the center. Namely, $Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ is also a graded $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ -algebra, which endows $\Spec_{\mathbb{A}^{1}\times Y}(Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}})$ with a natural $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action. Moreover, $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ is a graded $Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}}$ -algebra and as such defines a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras on the quotient stack $[\Spec_{\mathbb{A}^{1}\times Y}(Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{A}^{1}})/\mathbb{G}_{m}]$ .

#### Construction 3.4 (Rees construction over $\mathbb{S}=\mathbb{P}^{1}$ associated to two filtrations).

Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras over $Y$ endowed with two multiplicative and exhaustive filtrations $\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}*}$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{2}*}$ . We denote such data by $(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}*},\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{2}*})$ .

We cover $\mathbb{S}$ by two charts given by affine lines $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}\simeq\Spec\mathbb{Z}[h]$ and $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}\simeq\Spec\mathbb{Z}[h^{-1}]$ , with intersection given by $\mathbb{G}_{m}=\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\})\simeq\Spec\mathbb{Z}[h,h^{-1}]$ . On these charts we take Rees constructions associated to the two filtrations:

$$ \mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\coloneqq\oplus_{i}\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}i}\cdot h^{i}\subset\mathcal{B}[h,h^{-1}]\supset\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\coloneqq\oplus_{i}\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{2}i}\cdot h^{-i}. $$

$\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ are the $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h]$ and $\mathcal{O}_{Y}[h^{-1}]$ subalgebras of $\mathcal{B}[h,h^{-1}]$ and as such define quasicoherent sheaves of algebras on $(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\})\times Y$ and $(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\})\times Y$ correspondingly. Moreover, we have natural identifications

$$ {\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}|}_{(\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\}))\times Y}\simeq p^{*}\mathcal{B}\simeq{\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}|}_{(\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\}))\times Y} $$

between their restrictions to $(\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\}))\times Y$ . Using the composite isomorphism as the gluing data we obtain a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras on $\mathbb{S}\times Y$ which we will denote $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}}$ and call Rees construction over $\mathbb{P}^{1}$ .

There is also a version over the center of $\mathcal{B}$ . Namely, $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is naturally an algebra over $Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{S}}$ and thus defines a sheaf of algebras on $\Spec_{\ \!\!\mathbb{S}\times Y}Z(\mathcal{B})_{\mathbb{S}}$ which we will continue to denote $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}}$ .

#### Construction 3.5 (Descent to $[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]$ ).

Analogously to Construction 3.3 one endows algebras $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ with natural gradings $(\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}})^{i}\coloneqq\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}i}\cdot h^{i}$ and $(\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}})^{-i}\coloneqq\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}i}\cdot h^{-i}$ . This way they define quasi-coherent sheaves of algebras on $[(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\})/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y$ and $[(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\})/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y$ . Moreover, the restrictions of both $\mathcal{B}_{[\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}$ and $[\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]$ to $[(\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\}))/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y\simeq Y$ are naturally identified with $\mathcal{B}$ . This way we can glue them to a sheaf $\mathcal{B}_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}$ on $[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]_{Y}$ .

Similar construction works also over the center of $\mathcal{B}$ . Namely $\mathcal{B}_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}$ is naturally a sheaf of algebras over $Z(\mathcal{B})_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}$ and we can also consider $\mathcal{B}_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}$ as a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras over $\Spec_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]\times Y}(Z(\mathcal{B})_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]})$ .

#### Example 3.6 (Split case).

Assume $\mathcal{B}$ is commutative (so $\mathcal{B}\simeq Z(\mathcal{B})$ ). Let $\mathcal{B}$ be graded $\mathcal{B}\simeq\oplus_{i}\mathcal{B}_{i}$ and define the following two increasing filtrations associated to it:

$$ \mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}n}\coloneqq\oplus_{i\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{i}\text{ and }\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{2}n}\coloneqq\oplus_{i\geq-n}\mathcal{B}_{i}. $$

Then we claim that $\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}}$ splits: namely, one can identify $\Spec_{Y\times\mathbb{S}}(\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}})$ with $\Spec_{Y}(\mathcal{B})\times\mathbb{S}$ . Moreover, this isomorphism is $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -equivariant, where the $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action on $\Spec_{Y}(\mathcal{B})$ is defined by the grading we started with. This then also gives an isomorphism

$$ \Spec_{Y\times[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}(\mathcal{B}_{[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]})\simeq[(\Spec_{Y}(\mathcal{B})\times\mathbb{S})/\mathbb{G}_{m}]. $$

To see this, note that the $n$ -th graded component

$$ (\mathcal{B}[h])_{n}\simeq\oplus_{i+j=n}\mathcal{B}_{i}\cdot h^{j}\simeq\oplus_{i\leq n}\mathcal{B}_{i}\simeq\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{1}n} $$

and, this way $\mathcal{B}[h]\simeq\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ as a graded $\mathcal{O}_{Y}$ -algebra. Similarly,

$$ (\mathcal{B}[h^{-1}])_{n}\simeq\oplus_{i-j=n}\mathcal{B}_{i}\cdot h^{-j}\simeq\oplus_{i\geq-n}\mathcal{B}_{i}\simeq\mathcal{B}_{\leq^{2}n} $$

and $\mathcal{B}[h]\simeq\mathcal{B}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ . Moreover, under this identification the gluing data on the intersection $\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\})$ is just given by the isomorphism $(\mathcal{B}[h])[h^{-1}]\simeq(\mathcal{B}[h^{-1}])[h]$ . This way we can identify $\mathcal{B}_{S}$ with the pushforward $p_{*}\mathcal{O}$ for the projection $p\colon\Spec_{Y}\mathcal{B}\times\mathbb{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ , hence the statement above.

### 3.2. Twistor differential operators $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$

We now discuss a particular case of the above construction in the case of the sheaf of differential operators on a pseudo-smooth scheme. Let us clarify the setup.

#### Construction 3.7 (Hodge and conjugate filtrations on $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ ).

Namely, let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme and let $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ be the sheaf of differential operators that we have defined in Section 2.3. The pushforward $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ defines a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Let us discard $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ from the notation and implicitly consider $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ as a sheaf of algebras over $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Recall that we have an isomorphism $\theta^{-1}\colon Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})\simeq\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (see Corollary 2.38). Let us temporarily discard the subscript given by $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ to lighten up the notations.

We endow $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ with two filtrations:

- • (Hodge filtration). Consider filtration $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq*}\coloneqq\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq*}$ by the order of differential operator (see Remark 2.18). One has $\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq n}=0$ if $n<0$ and $\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq 0}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X}$ :

$$ \ldots=0=0\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq 1}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X,\leq 2}\subset\ldots $$

- • (Conjugate filtration). This is a filtration $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq*}$ defined as follows. Namely one has $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq n}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{X}$ if $n\geq 0$ :

$$ \ldots\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq-2}\subset\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq-1}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X}=\mathcal{D}_{X}=\ldots $$

and $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq-i}$ is defined as $\Sym^{\lfloor\frac{i}{p}\rfloor}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\cdot\mathcal{D}_{X}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X}$ . In particular, it is a $p$ -step filtration (one has $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq-i}=\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq-i+1}$ unless $p|i$ ).

#### Remark 3.8.

The conjugate filtration $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq*}$ is a reindexed variant of a filtration that appeard in [OV].

#### Remark 3.9 (Induced filtrations on the center).

Filtrations induced on $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ by the Hodge and conjugate filtrations on $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ above are in fact split. Namely, we claim that the two filtrations $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})\cap\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq*}$ and $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})\cap\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq*}$ are obtained by construction in Example 3.6 from the single grading on $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ given as follows:

$$ Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{n}\coloneqq\begin{cases}0&\text{if $p\nmid n$}\\
\Sym^{k}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}&\text{if $n=p\cdot k$}\end{cases} $$

This is clear for the conjugate filtration: since $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})\cap\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq-n}$ is given by $\Sym^{\geq[\frac{n}{p}]}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ which is also a direct sum $\oplus_{i}Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{i}$ with $i\geq n$ . For the Hodge filtration this requires a slight argument.

More precisely, we need to show that $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq n}\cap Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})\simeq\Sym^{\leq[\frac{n}{p}]}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (where the latter is isomorphic to $\oplus_{i}Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{i}$ with $i\geq n$ ). Recall that the map $\theta\colon\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ is induced by $v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mapsto\theta(v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\colon v^{p}-v^{[p]}$ and so $\theta(\mathcal{T}_{X})\subset\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq p}$ . Consequently, $\theta(\Sym^{\leq k}\mathcal{T}_{X})\subset\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq pk}$ and to show the statement it is enough enough to show that the map $\gr_{pk}\theta\colon\Sym^{k}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\mathrm{gr}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq pk}$ between the associated graded pieces is an embedding. We have $\theta(v^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})=v^{p}\in\gr_{p}^{\mathrm{H}}$ and this way we see that the map of $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -algebras $\gr_{*}(\theta)\colon\Sym^{*}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\!\!\mathcal{T}_{X}$ is the map given by reduced Frobenius $F_{T^{*}\!X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon T^{*}\!X\rightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ (as affine schemes over $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ ), which is an embedding essentially by definition.

Following the discussion in Example 3.6 we then get the following description of the Rees construction for $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ . Namely, the grading on $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ that we considered above corresponds to the $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action on $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Spec_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ where $t\in\mathbb{G}_{m}$ acts by rescaling the fibers of the vector bundle $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ by $t^{p}$ . We get a $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -equivariant isomorphism

$$ \Spec_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\times\mathbb{S}}Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{\ \!\!\mathbb{S}}\simeq(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{S}, $$

where the action on the right is diagonal.

It then also descends to an isomorphism

$$ \Spec_{X^{\!{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\times[\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{\ \!\![\mathbb{S}/\mathbb{G}_{m}]}\simeq[((T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{S})/\mathbb{G}_{m}]. $$

for the corresponding quotients by $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ .

#### Definition 3.10 (Twistor differential operators).

We define the sheaf $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ of twistor differential operators on $X$ as the Rees construction (3.4) over $\mathbb{S}$ associated to $(\mathcal{D}_{X},\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{H}}_{\leq*},\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq*})$ . By Remark 3.9 and discussion in Example 3.6, $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ defines a $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -equivariant quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\!\times\mathbb{S}$ (where the relevant $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -action on the latter is discussed in the end of Remark 3.9).

#### Remark 3.11.

Let us describe $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ more explicitly. Namely, the restriction $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ is the Rees algebra associated to PBW-filtration on $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ and as such can be identified with the subalgebra in $\mathcal{D}_{X}[h]$ generated by $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $h\cdot\mathcal{T}_{X}$ .
