Following Remark 3.9 and Example 3.6 we have an isomorphism ${Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})[h]\simeq(\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\!\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})[h]$ . The corresponding map ${Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ sends $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ to $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ via $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , while $v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ maps to1919 19 To see why this is the formula: we have $\theta(v)\in\mathrm{Fil}_{\leq p}^{\mathrm{H}}$ and $\theta(v)\cdot h^{p}=v^{p}h^{p}-v^{[p]}h^{p}=(vh)^{p}-h^{p-1}(v^{[p]}h)$ . $\theta_{h}(v)=v^{p}-h^{p-1}\cdot v^{[p]}$ .

For the description of the other chart note that since $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq 0}=\mathcal{D}_{X}$ we have a natural embedding $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})[h^{-1}]\subset{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ . Moreover, by the way how $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{cnj}}_{\leq*}$ is defined, $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ is identified with the tensor product $\mathcal{D}_{X}[h^{-1}]\otimes_{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})[h^{-1}]}{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ . Note that over $\{\infty\}\in\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ the map $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})[h^{-1}]/h^{-1}\rightarrow{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}/h^{-1}$ is given by the composition

$$ \Sym^{*}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\Sym^{*}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}} $$

where the first map is the projection. This way $\mathcal{D}_{X,\{\infty\}}\coloneqq\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}/h^{-1}$ is identified with $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\Sym^{*}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ where $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}$ is the central reduction from Remark 2.29. Recall that $\mathcal{D}_{X,0}\simeq\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\mathcal{O}_{X})$ is a split Azumaya algebra; this way $\mathcal{D}_{X,\{\infty\}}$ is Morita equivalent to $\mathcal{O}_{X}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\Sym^{*}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Sym_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}\mathcal{T}_{X}$ . In particular, the category of quasi-coherent sheaves of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\{\infty\}}$ -modules is equivalent to quasi-coherent sheaves over $T^{*}\!X$ .

The two restrictions $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ and $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ are then glued along $\mathbb{S}\backslash(\{0\}\sqcup\{\infty\})$ via identification of the restrictions of both algebras with $\mathcal{D}_{X}[h,h^{-1}]$ .

Let $\mu\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X/S})$ be a closed $1$ -form on $X$ . Define an automorphism $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}$ of algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ (viewed as the subalgebra of $\mathcal{D}_{X}[h]$ generated by $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $h\cdot\mathcal{T}_{X}$ ) by setting $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}(f)=f$ and $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}(hv)=hv+\iota_{v}\mu$ , for every function $f$ and every vector field $v$ . Informally, this automorphism is the conjugation by $e^{\frac{1}{h}\int\mu}$ : though this expression does not make sense as a function on $X\times\mathbb{S}$ , the conjugation automorphism is well defined. For $\mu_{1},\mu_{2}\in H^{0}(X,\Omega^{1}_{X/S})$ , we have that

$$ \phi_{\frac{\mu_{1}}{h}}\circ\phi_{\frac{\mu_{2}}{h}}=\phi_{\frac{\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}}{h}}. $$

The action of $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}$ on the center $(\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\!\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})[h]$ of the algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ is given by the Katz $p$ -curvature formula (see Remark 2.43): $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}$ acts trivially on $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and, for $v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , one has that $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}(h^{p}v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})=h^{p}v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}+\iota_{v^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\mu^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}-h^{p-1}C(\mu)).$ In particular, if $C(\mu)=0$ i.e., $\mu$ is exact, then $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}$ extends to an automorphism of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ and acts on the spectrum of its centre $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{S}$ as the translation by $\mu^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

Now we extend Construction 2.44 to the algebra of twistor differential operators. Let $\alpha\in H^{0}(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X})$ be a global section, $i_{\alpha}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ the graph of $\alpha$ . Denote by

$$ \mathcal{I}_{\alpha,\mathbb{S}}\subset Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{\ \!\!\mathbb{S}}\subset\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}} $$

the sheaf of ideals determined by the closed embedding $i_{\alpha}\times\Id_{\mathbb{S}}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\mathbb{S}$ . Let $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{\alpha}{h^{p}},\mathbb{S}}$ be the quotient $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}/\mathcal{I}_{\alpha,\mathbb{S}}\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ .

For an exact $1$ -form $\mu$ on $X$ , one has that $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}(\mathcal{I}_{\alpha,\mathbb{S}})=\mathcal{I}_{\alpha+\mu^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\mathbb{S}}$ . It follows that $\phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}$ descends to an isomorphism:

$$ \phi_{\frac{\mu}{h}}\colon\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{\alpha}{h^{p}},\mathbb{S}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{\alpha+\mu^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}{h^{p}},\mathbb{S}}. $$

#### Construction 3.12 (Central reduction of twistor differential operators).

A class

$$ [\eta]\in H_{Zar}^{0}\left(X,\operatorname{coker}\left(\mathcal{O}_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega_{X/S}^{1}\right)\right) $$

gives rise to a certain central reduction $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ of the algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ . This is a sheaf of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -algebras that comes together with the following structure. For any open subset $U$ together with a $1$ -form $\eta\in\Omega^{1}_{X/S}(U)$ representing $[\eta]$ , we have an isomorphism of $\mathcal{O}_{U}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -algebras

$$ \gamma_{U,\eta}\colon(\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}})_{|U}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\mathcal{D}_{U,\frac{(\eta_{|U})^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}{h^{p}},\mathbb{S}} $$

such that, for any two $1$ -forms $\eta_{1}$ , $\eta_{2}$ on $U$ representing the class $[\eta]$ , one has that $\gamma_{U,\eta_{2}}\circ\gamma_{U,\eta_{1}}^{-1}=\phi_{\eta_{2}-\eta_{1}}.$ Formula (3.2) shows that the algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ together with the collections of $\gamma_{U,\eta}$ exists and is unique up to a unique isomorphisms. Moreover, the construction is functorial meaning that the sheaf algebras $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ is equivariant with respect to the group $\Aut_{S}(X,[\eta])$ of automorphisms of $X$ over $S$ preserving the class $[\eta]$ . For future reference we display the induced action $\Aut_{S}(X,[\eta])$ on the direct image $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ along the projection $\pro_{S\times\mathbb{S}}\colon X\times\mathbb{S}\to S\times\mathbb{S}$ by ${\mathcal{O}}_{S\times\mathbb{S}}$ -algebra automorphisms

$$ \psi\colon\Aut_{\mathbb{S}}(X,[\eta])\to\Aut(\pro_{\mathbb{S}*}\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}). $$

The algebra $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ has further symmetries. Endow $\mathbb{S}$ with an action $\chi$ of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ by homotheties: $\chi(h)=zh$ , where $z$ is the coordinate on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Then pullback of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ with respect to the morphism ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\times\mathbb{S}\to X\times\mathbb{S}$ given by the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action on the last factor is naturally isomorphic to $\mathcal{D}_{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X,\frac{[z^{-1}\pro_{X}^{*}\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ , where $\pro_{X}\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\to X$ is the projection.

#### Example 3.13 (The sheaf $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}}$ ).

Let’s consider a particular case of the above construction when we have $[\eta]=0$ . The corresponding sheaf of algebras $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}}$ is simply the restriction of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}$ to the zero section $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\!\times\mathbb{S}\rightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\!\times\mathbb{S}$ , or in terms of sheaves of algebras we have $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}}\otimes_{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})_{\mathbb{S}}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}.$

Let us describe more explicitly the gluing data corresponding to $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}}$ . Namely, $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ is given by the quotient of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ (which is generated by $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ modulo the relations as in Remark 3.11) by the two-sided ideal generated by $v^{p}-h^{p-1}v^{[p]}$ , $v\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ . On the other hand, restriction $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ is really simple, namely $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{X,0}[h^{-1}]$ . Indeed, by Remark 3.11 $\mathcal{D}_{X,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{X}[h^{-1}]\otimes_{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})[h^{-1}]}{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ from which we get that

$$ \mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{X}[h^{-1}]\otimes_{Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})[h^{-1}]}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}[h^{-1}]\simeq\mathcal{D}_{X,0}[h^{-1}]. $$

Observe that, for every class $[\eta]$ the restriction of $\mathcal{D}_{X,\frac{[\eta]}{h},\mathbb{S}}$ to $X\times\{\infty\}\hookrightarrow X\times\mathbb{S}$ is naturally isomorphic to that of $\mathcal{D}_{X,0,\mathbb{S}}$ . In particular, the former is a canonically split Azumaya algebra over $X\times\{\infty\}$ .

### 3.3. Twistor reduced Weyl algebra $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$

We will be now interested in a very particular case of the Construction 3.12. Namely, let us fix a number $n\in\mathbb{N}$ . Consider the algebra $C\coloneqq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}]/(x_{1}^{p},\ldots,x_{n}^{p})$ : this is the (ring of functions on the) Frobenius neighborhood of $\{0\}$ in an $n$ -dimensional affine space over $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ . Put $Y\coloneqq\Spec C$ . This is a pseudo-smooth $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -scheme (with $\Omega^{1}_{C}\simeq\oplus_{i=1}^{n}C\cdot dx_{i}$ ) and one has $Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Spec(C^{p})\simeq\Spec\mathbb{F}_{p}$ .

#### Definition 3.14.

We define the twistor reduced Weyl algebra $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ as $\mathcal{D}_{Y,0,\mathbb{S}}$ . This is a quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras on $\mathbb{S}$ .

#### Remark 3.15.

Note that by (the proof of) Lemma 2.67 any pseudo-smooth $X$ looks like $C$ flat locally over its Frobenius twist $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . This way $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ can serve as a model example of quantization (in this context of $T^{*}\!X$ ).

Let us describe $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ in terms of its restrictions to $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}$ and $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ and the gluing data. First, let us describe the algebra $D_{Y}=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal{D}_{Y})$ . We have $\mathcal{T}_{Y}\simeq\oplus_{i=1}^{n}C\cdot\partial_{i}$ with $\partial_{i}(x_{j})=\delta_{ij}$ . Thus

$$ D_{Y}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}\langle x_{i},y_{j}\rangle_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/([x_{i},x_{j}]=[y_{i},y_{j}]=x_{i}^{p}=0,[y_{j},x_{j}]=\delta_{ij}) $$

with $y_{i}$ corresponding to $\partial_{i}$ . One sees easily that $\partial_{i}^{[p]}=0$ and so the center $Z(D_{Y})$ is described as

$$ Z(D_{Y})\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[y_{1}^{p},\ldots,y_{n}^{p}]\subset D_{Y}. $$

Hodge filtration on $D_{Y}$ is given by the total degree in $y_{i}$ ’s. Following Remark 3.11 the corresponding Rees algebra $D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ is the $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra given by

$$ D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]\langle x_{i},y_{j}\rangle_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/([x_{i},x_{j}]=[y_{i},y_{j}]=x_{i}^{p}=0,[y_{j},x_{j}]=h\cdot\delta_{ij}) $$

The center $Z(D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}})$ is identified with

$$ Z(D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}})\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h,y_{1}^{p},\ldots,y_{n}^{p}]\subset D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}. $$

We have $D_{Y,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\coloneqq D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\otimes_{Z(D_{Y,\mathbb{S}\backslash\infty})}\mathbb{F}_{p}$ and so

$$ D_{Y,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]\langle x_{i},y_{j}\rangle_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/([x_{i},x_{j}]=[y_{i},y_{j}]=y_{j}^{p}=x_{i}^{p}=0,[y_{j},x_{j}]=h\cdot\delta_{ij}). $$

Finally, $D_{Y,0}\coloneqq D_{Y}\otimes_{Z(D_{Y})}\mathcal{O}(Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is described as

$$ D_{Y,0}\coloneqq\mathbb{F}_{p}\langle x_{i},y_{j}\rangle_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/([x_{i},x_{j}]=[y_{i},y_{j}]=x_{i}^{p}=y_{j}^{p}=0,[y_{j},x_{j}]=\delta_{ij}) $$

Following Remark 2.29 the natural action of $D_{Y,0}$ on $C$ (where $x_{i}$ acts by multiplication and $y_{i}$ by $\partial_{i}$ ) produces an isomorphism

$$ D_{Y,0}\simeq\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}(C)\simeq\Mat_{p^{n}}(\mathbb{F}_{p}). $$

#### Remark 3.16 (Explicit description of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ ).

Now, following Example 3.13 we can explicitly describe $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . Let $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ be the restriction of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ to the corresponding charts. We have $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{Y,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ and so the $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\coloneqq\Gamma(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\},\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}})$ is described as

$$ A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]\langle x_{i},y_{j}\rangle_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/([x_{i},x_{j}]=[y_{i},y_{j}]=y_{j}^{p}=x_{i}^{p}=0,[y_{j},x_{j}]=h\cdot\delta_{ij}). $$

We note that $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ is a free $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -module of rank $p^{2n}$ (by ordered monomials $x^{I}y^{J}$ with the degrees less or equal than $p-1$ in each variable).

On the other hand, $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{Y,0,\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\mathcal{D}_{Y,0}[h^{-1}]$ , and so by the above the $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h^{-1}]$ -algebra $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\coloneqq\Gamma(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\},\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}})$ is given by

$$ A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h^{-1}]\langle x^{\prime}_{i},y_{j}^{\prime}\rangle_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/([x^{\prime}_{i},x_{j}^{\prime}]=[y_{i}^{\prime},y_{j}^{\prime}]=x_{i}^{\prime p}=y_{j}^{\prime p}=0,[y_{j}^{\prime},x_{j}^{\prime}]=\delta_{ij}). $$

Similarly, this is a free $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h^{-1}]$ -module of rank $p^{2n}$ . It follows that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is locally free as an $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{S}}$ -module of rank $p^{2n}$ . The identification $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}[h^{-1}]\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}[h]$ is given by $x_{i}=x^{\prime}_{i}$ and $y_{i}=h\cdot y_{i}^{\prime}$ (since $y_{i}$ and $y_{i}^{\prime}$ in fact corresponds to $h\cdot\partial_{i}$ and $\partial_{i}$ ).

#### Remark 3.17.

Since $D_{Y,0}\simeq\Mat_{p^{n}}(\mathbb{F}_{p})$ we get that $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\simeq\Mat_{p^{n}}(\mathbb{F}_{p})[h^{-1}]$ . Also $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ embeds into $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}[h^{-1}]\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}[h]\simeq\Mat_{p^{n}}(\mathbb{F}_{p})[h,h^{-1}]$ so $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is an order in a matrix algebra of rank $p^{n}$ over $\mathbb{S}$ .

#### Construction 3.18 (A module over ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ ).

We define a sheaf ${\mathcal{V}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ of ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ -modules as follows. As an ${\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ -module ${\mathcal{V}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is free:

$$ {\mathcal{V}}_{\mathbb{S}}={\mathcal{O}}_{\mathbb{S}}\otimes{\mathbb{F}}_{p}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n}]/(x_{i}^{p},1\leq i\leq n). $$

The action of $x_{i}\in\Gamma({\mathbb{S}},{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})$ on ${\mathcal{V}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ is given by the multiplication on the right factor; the action of $y_{i}\in\Gamma(\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\},{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})$ is given by the formula $y_{i}(f)=h\otimes\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_{i}}$ , for $f\in{\mathbb{F}}_{p}[x_{1},\cdots,x_{n}]/(x_{i}^{p},1\leq i\leq n)$ .

### 3.4. Algebra $A_{0}$

Let $i_{0}\colon\{0\}\simeq\Spec\mathbb{F}_{p}\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ be an embedding of 0.

#### Definition 3.19.

We define the $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra $A_{0}$ as $i_{0}^{*}\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . Equivalently, $A_{0}\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h$ and so (using Remark 3.16)

$$ A_{0}\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x_{i},y_{j}]_{1\leq i,j\leq n}/(x_{i}^{p}=y_{j}^{p}=0). $$

We also let $A_{h}$ to be the $h$ -adic completion of the $k[h]$ -algebra $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ . Since $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}$ is finitely-generated as a $k[h]$ -module one has $A_{h}\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\otimes_{k[h]}k[[h]].$

For an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra $R$ we will denote by $A_{0}(R)$ the $R$ -algebra $A_{0}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}R$ . Note that $\Spec A_{0}(R)$ is pseudo-smooth over $R$ for any $R$ .

#### Construction 3.20.

We denote by $\ev_{0}\colon A_{0}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb{F}_{p}$ the “evaluation at 0”-map that sends all $x_{i}$ and $y_{j}$ to 0. We let $I_{0}\coloneqq\Ker(\ev_{0})\subset A_{0}$ be the ideal given by its kernel. Obviously, $I_{0}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n},y_{1},\ldots,y_{n})$ . For any $R$ we put $I_{0}(R)\coloneqq I_{0}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}R\subset A_{0}(R)$ . Note that $I_{0}(R)\subset\alpha_{p}(A_{0}(R))$ .

Let us now apply some of the results of Section 2 to $S\coloneqq\Spec R$ and $X\coloneqq\Spec A_{0}(R)$ . Following Example 2.11(2) we have $A_{0}(R)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq R\subset A_{0}(R)$ ; this way the reduced Frobenius map $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is identified with the projection $X\rightarrow S$ . On the other hand since $x_{i}^{p}=y_{j}^{p}=0$ the reduced twist map $W_{A_{0}(R)}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon A_{0}(R)\rightarrow R$ induced by $a\mapsto a^{p}\in R\simeq A_{0}(R)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is identified with the composition $A_{0}(R)\xrightarrow{\ev_{0}}R\xrightarrow{-^{p}}R$ , $a\mapsto\ev_{0}(a)^{p}$ .

Consider the $A_{0}(R)$ -module $\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}\coloneqq\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)/R}$ of $R$ -relative differential 1-forms. $\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is a free $A_{0}(R)$ -module of rank $2n$ spanned by $dx_{i}$ and $dy_{i}$ for $i=1,\dots,n$ . Consider also the $R$ -module $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}\coloneqq\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}\otimes_{A_{0}(R),\ev_{0}^{p}}R$ . We let $\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}\subset\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}$ be the $R$ -module of closed 1-forms. We have the de Rham differential $A_{0}(R)\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}$ and the Cartier operation $\mathsf{C}\colon\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ .

#### Lemma 3.21.

There is a short exact sequence of $R$ -modules

$$ 0\rightarrow A_{0}(R)/R\xrightarrow{d}\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}\xrightarrow{\mathsf{C}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}\rightarrow 0 $$

#### Proof.

This follows by applying global sections to the Cartier short exact sequence (2.3) on the affine $R$ -scheme $X=\Spec A_{0}(R)$ . ∎

#### Remark 3.22.

Under an isomorphism

$$ \Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}\simeq\left(\oplus_{i=1}^{n}R\cdot dx_{i}\right)\oplus\left(\oplus_{i=1}^{n}R\cdot d{y_{i}}\right), $$

the Cartier operation has the following description. Namely, given $\alpha\in\Omega^{1}_{X/R,cl}$ we need to write it as a sum of monomials in $x_{i},y_{j}$ times $dx_{k},dy_{l}$ with coefficients in $R$ and look at the coefficients $a_{i}\in R$ and $b_{j}\in R^{\prime}$ in front of summands of the form $x_{i}^{p-1}dx_{i}$ and $y_{j}^{p-1}dy_{j}$ . Then $\mathsf{C}(\alpha)=\sum_{i}a_{i}\cdot{dx_{i}}+\sum_{j}b_{j}\cdot{dy_{j}}\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}.$

We can also consider maps $d\log\colon A_{0}(R)^{\times}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}$ and the map $-^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ sending $\alpha$ to $\alpha\otimes 1\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ .

#### Lemma 3.23.

There is a short exact sequence

$$ 0\rightarrow A_{0}(R)^{\times}/R^{\times}\xrightarrow{d\log}\Omega^{1,cl}_{A_{0}(R)}\xrightarrow{\alpha\mapsto\mathsf{C}(\alpha)-\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}\rightarrow 0. $$

#### Proof.

Let $X\coloneqq\Spec A_{0}(R)$ . By Example 2.11, $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq S\coloneqq\Spec R$ . Recall Milne’s exact sequence (Proposition 2.46). We claim that $H^{1}_{\text{et}}(S,F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}/\mathcal{O}_{S}^{\times})=0$ . Indeed, by Remark 3.24 below, $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}$ splits as $\mathcal{O}_{S}^{\times}\times(1+I_{0})^{\times}$ and $H^{1}_{\text{et}}(S,(1+I_{0})^{\times})$ is 0. The other terms in Milne’s exact sequence are coherent sheaves, and so also don’t have higher cohomology. Thus, applying global sections to 2.46 we exactly get (3.4) above. ∎

#### Remark 3.24.

Recall the ideal $I_{0}(R)\coloneqq\Ker(\ev_{0})$ . Consider the subgroup $(1+I_{0}(R))^{\times}\subset A_{0}(R)^{\times}$ : since $I_{0}(R)$ lies in the nilradical of $A_{0}(R)$ it is well-defined, and identifies with the kernel of the map $A_{0}(R)^{\times}\twoheadrightarrow R^{\times}$ induced by $\ev_{0}$ . Together with the map $R^{\times}\rightarrow A_{0}(R)^{\times}$ this gives a splitting $A_{0}(R)^{\times}\simeq R^{\times}\times(1+I_{0}(R))$ functorially in $R$ . Moreover, $(1+I_{0}(R))$ has a functorial in $R$ ) finite filtration by

$$ (1+I_{0}(R))^{\times}\supset(1+I_{0}(R)^{2})^{\times}\supset(1+I_{0}(R)^{3})^{\times}+\ldots $$

with $(1+I_{0}(R)^{n})/(1+I_{0}(R)^{n+1})\simeq I_{0}(R)^{n}/I_{0}(R)^{n+1}$ which is a free $R$ -module spanned by monomials in $x_{i}$ ’s and $y_{j}$ ’s of degree $n$ .

This shows that the étale sheaf $(1+I_{0})^{\times}\colon R\mapsto(1+I_{0}(R))^{\times}$ on the bog site of affine $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -schemes has a finite filtration with the associated graded given by a coherent sheaf. In particular, for any specific $\Spec R$ the restriction of this sheaf to the small étale site $(\Spec R)_{\text{et}}$ doesn’t have higher cohomology: $H^{>0}_{\text{et}}(\Spec R,(1+I_{0})^{\times})=0$

#### Construction 3.25 (Restricted structure on the Frobenius neighborhood).

We endow $X=\Spec A_{0}(R)$ with the structure of a restricted symplectic $R$ -scheme as in Construction 2.63. Namely, we consider $(X,[\eta_{\mathsf{can}}])$ with

$$ \eta_{\mathsf{can}}\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_{i}dx_{i}\in\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}. $$

The corresponding symplectic from is given by $\omega\coloneqq d\eta_{\mathsf{can}}=\sum_{i}dy_{i}\wedge dx_{i}\in\Omega^{2}_{A_{0}(R)}$ .

For the lemma that will follow shortly we will need the following generalization of Definition 2.58.

#### Definition 3.26.

Let $X$ be a symplectic $S$ -scheme. A derivation $\xi\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{T}_{X})$ is called $\log$ -Hamiltonian if $\xi=f^{-1}\cdot H_{f}$ for some $f\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times})$ .

#### Remark 3.27.

Similarly to the Hamiltonian case, the condition $\xi=f^{-1}\cdot H_{f}$ is equivalent to $\iota_{\xi}\omega=d\log f$ .

Given a vector field $\xi\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{T}_{X})$ we denote by $L_{\xi}\colon\Omega^{i}_{X}\rightarrow\Omega^{i}_{X}$ the Lie derivative along $\xi$ . We recall the Cartan formula: $L_{\xi}=\iota_{\xi}\circ d+d\circ\iota_{\xi}$ in terms of the de Rham differential and contraction. A vector field $\xi$ is called Poisson if $L_{\xi}\omega=0$ .

#### Lemma 3.28.

- (1) A Poisson vector field $\xi\in{\mathcal{T}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is Hamiltonian if and only if for all $f\in A_{0}(R)$ we have

$$ \xi(f^{[p]})=H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f)). $$

- (2) A Poisson derivation $\xi\in{\mathcal{T}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is $\log$ -Hamiltonian if and only if for all $f\in A$ we have (3.5)

$$ \xi(f^{[p]})=H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f))\ +\ \xi(f)^{p}. $$

#### Proof.

The proof essentially follows [BK, Lemma 2.5]. By Cartan formula and the assumption $L_{\xi}\omega=0\Rightarrow d(\iota_{\xi}\omega)+0=0$ we get that $\beta\coloneqq\iota_{\xi}\omega\in\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is closed. By Remark 2.59 and Lemma 3.21 $\xi$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $\mathsf{C}(\beta)=0$ . Similarly, by Lemma 3.23 $\xi$ is $\log$ -Hamiltonian if and only if $\mathsf{C}(\beta)=\beta^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Since $\omega$ is non-degenerate, Hamiltonian vector fields generate $\mathcal{T}_{A_{0}(R)}$ . Then vector fields of the form $H_{f}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ generate $\mathcal{T}_{A_{0}(R)}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , and so it is enough to understand the pairing of $\mathsf{C}(\beta)\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ with (the twists of) Hamiltonian vector fields. By Remark 2.41 $\iota_{H_{f}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\mathsf{C}(\beta))=\langle H_{f}^{[p]},\beta\rangle-H_{f}^{p-1}(\langle{H_{f}},\beta\rangle)$ . Substituting $\beta=\iota_{\xi}\omega$ we get $\iota_{H_{f}}(\mathsf{C}(\beta))=\xi(f^{[p]})-H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f))\in R\subset A_{0}(R)$ . Thus, $\mathsf{C}(\beta)=0$ if and only if $\xi(f^{[p]})-H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f))=0$ for all $f\in A_{0}(R)$ . This gives Part 1. Part 2 is obtained similarly, by noting that $\iota_{H_{f}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\beta^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})=(\iota_{H_{f}}\beta)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}=\xi(f)^{p}$ . ∎

### 3.5. $h$ -separable algebras

Let $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ be the category of schemes over $\mathbb{S}$ . To construct a group action on the category of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ -modules it will be crucial to have some understanding of the algebra automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . This will become easier if we restrict to a certain subcategory in $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ , where automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ are closely related to $G_{0}$ . The goal of this section is to define this subcategory.

#### Construction 3.29.

Let $R\in\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}$ . For an element $b\in R/h$ let $\tilde{b}\in R$ be a lift. Then the operation $b\mapsto\tilde{b}^{p}$ gives a well-defined map $R/h\rightarrow R/h^{p}$ . Indeed, given other lift $\tilde{b}^{\prime}=\tilde{b}+hc$ we have $(\tilde{b}^{\prime})^{p}=\tilde{b}^{p}+h^{p}c^{p}$ .

Consider $\alpha_{p}(R/h)=\{a\in R/h\ |\ a^{p}=0\}\subset R/h$ . Then restricting the above map to $\alpha_{p}(R/h)$ gives a map $\delta\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R$ .

#### Definition 3.30.

An $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra $R$ is called $h$ -separable if

- (1) it is $h$ -torsion free (equivalently, flat over $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ );

- (2) the map $\delta_{R}\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R$ is equal to 0.

#### Remark 3.31.

It is not hard to see that the latter condition is equivalent to the following: for any $a\in R$ one has

$$ a^{p}\in hR\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad a^{p}\in h^{p}R. $$

We denote by $\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}}$ the category of $h$ -separable $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebras.

#### Example 3.32.

- (1) Let $C$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra. Then $R\coloneqq C\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ is $h$ -separable. Indeed, it is $h$ -torsion free and to check the second condition note that $R/h\simeq C$ and any $x\in\alpha_{p}(R/h)$ can be lifted to $x\otimes 1$ for which $(x\otimes 1)^{p}=x^{p}\otimes 1=0$ . Thus $\delta_{R}$ is 0.

- (2) Any $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h,h^{-1}]$ -algebra $R$ is $h$ -separable. Indeed, it is obviously $h$ -tosion free and the second condition is vacuous since $R/h=0$ .

- (3) $R\coloneqq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h^{1/p}]$ is not $h$ separable. Indeed, $R/h\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]/x^{p}$ where $x$ is the class of $h^{1/p}$ , and the map $\delta_{R}$ sends $x$ to $h\in hR/h^{p}R$ .

Note that $\alpha_{p}(R/h)$ has a natural structure of $R$ -module such that $\delta_{R}$ is a Frobenius-linear map of $R$ -modules. Let $\delta_{R}^{\ell}\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\otimes_{R,F_{R}}R\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R$ be its linearization. Obviously, $\delta_{R}=0\Leftrightarrow\delta_{R}^{\ell}=0$ .

Even though it might not yet be clear what is the motivation behind the notion $h$ -separability, let us show that it is local in étale topology:

#### Lemma 3.33.

Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra and let $R\rightarrow R^{\prime}$ be an étale cover. Then $R$ is $h$ -separable if and only if $R^{\prime}$ is.

#### Proof.

$R^{\prime}$ is faithfully flat over $R$ , and so $R$ is $h$ -torsion free if and only if so is $R^{\prime}$ . It remains to relate $\delta_{R}$ and $\delta_{R^{\prime}}$ . Since $R\rightarrow R^{\prime}$ is étale, the relative Frobenius $F_{R^{\prime}/R}$ is an isomorphism. We have a factorization

#### Definition 3.35.

A $\mathbb{S}$ -scheme $X\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ is called $h$ -separable if its base change to $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}$ has a Zariski cover by $\{U_{i}\coloneqq\Spec R_{i}\}$ where each $R_{i}$ is a separable $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra.

#### Example 3.36.

- (1) If the map $X\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ factors through $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ then $X$ is $h$ -separable. Indeed, in this case $X_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ can be covered by spectra of $\mathbb{F}[h,h^{-1}]$ -algebras that are $h$ -separated.

- (2) Let $R$ be an $h$ -separable $k[h]$ -algebra. Then the composition $\Spec R\rightarrow\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ defines an $h$ -separable $\mathbb{S}$ -scheme.

We consider the big site $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}\subset\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ of all $h$ -separable schemes over $\mathbb{S}$ endowed with the étale topology2020 20 In fact for all the computations we will only need to use Zariski topology, but we just wanted to point out that étale topology also make sense in this setup..

### 3.6. Automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$

We let ${\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})$ be the sheaf on big fpqc site of $\mathbb{S}$ which sends $f\colon X\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ to algebra automorphisms of $f^{*}\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . Given the explicit description of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ in Remark 3.16 one sees that ${\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})$ is represented by a finite type group scheme over $\mathbb{S}$ . The first goal of this section is to show that if we restrict to $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}\subset\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ the map $i_{0}^{*}\colon{\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})\rightarrow i_{0*}(\underline{\Aut}(A_{0}))$ above factors through $i_{0*}G_{0}$ .

The key is to reinterpret the restricted Poisson structure on $A_{0}(R/h)$ in terms of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ . Note that (since $A_{0}\coloneqq i_{0}^{*}\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ ) we have $A_{0}(R/h)\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h$ .

#### Remark 3.38 (Poisson structure).

Let $R$ be $h$ -torsion free. Then $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is $h$ -torsion free as well and we can identify $h^{i}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{i+1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\simeq A_{0}(R/h)$ (via dividing by $h^{i}$ ) for any $i\geq 0$ . For an element $f\in A_{0}(R/h)$ let $\tilde{f}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ denote a lift under the projection $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\twoheadrightarrow A_{0}(R/h)$ . One can define a Poisson bracket $\{-,-\}$ on $A_{0}(R/h)$ by the equation $h\{f,g\}=[\tilde{f},\tilde{g}]\pmod{h^{2}}$ . One sees immediately from the relations defining $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ that $\{x_{i},x_{j}\}=\{y_{i},y_{j}\}=0$ , while $\{y_{j},x_{i}\}=\delta_{ij}$ and so this Poisson structure agrees with the one defined by $\omega$ (see Construction 3.25).

The restricted $p$ -th power operation $-^{[p]}$ (corresponding to the restricted Poisson structure on $A_{0}(R)$ ) is more subtle to identify and this is where $h$ -separability property is important.

#### Construction 3.39 (Restricted structure).

Note that for any $f\in A_{0}(R/h)$ and any lift $\tilde{f}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ the expression $\tilde{f}^{p}$ is well-defined mod $h^{p}$ . Indeed, by the Jacobson’s formula (see Section 2.2) we have

$$ (\tilde{f}+h\tilde{g})^{p}=\tilde{f}^{p}+h^{p}\tilde{g}^{p}+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}h^{i}L_{i}(\tilde{f},\tilde{g}), $$

where each $L_{i}(\tilde{f},\tilde{g})$ is a Lie polynomial of total degree $p-1$ . Since the commutator $[A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R),A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)]\subset hA_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ we get that $h^{i}L_{i}(\tilde{f},\tilde{g})\in h^{p-1+i}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ , and, consequently, that $(\tilde{f}+h\tilde{g})^{p}=\tilde{f}^{p}\pmod{h^{p}}$ .

Recall the map $\mathsf{s}\colon(R/h)^{p}\rightarrow R/h^{p}$ that we constructed in Remark 3.34. We will denote in the same way its composition with the embedding $R/h^{p}\hookrightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{p}$ . The $p$ -restricted structure then appears as follows, namely for any $f\in A_{0}(R/h)$ and a lift $\tilde{f}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ one can show as in Lemma 2.51 that the difference $\tilde{f}^{p}-\mathsf{s}(\ev_{0}(f)^{p})$ is divisible by $h^{p-1}$ and define

$$ h^{p-1}\cdot f^{[p]}\coloneqq\tilde{f}^{p}-\mathsf{s}(\ev_{0}(f)^{p})\pmod{h^{p}}. $$

Here we implicitly identified $h^{p-1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{p}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\simeq A_{0}(R/h)$ and considered $s(\ev_{0}(f)^{p})$ as an element of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{p}$ . By the same argument as in Lemma 2.51, one sees that this defines a restricted Poisson structure on $A_{0}(R/h)$ which coincides with the one that we defined in Construction 3.25 by Lemma 3.41 below.

#### Lemma 3.41.

The restricted structures on $A_{0}(R/h)$ from Constructions 3.39 and 3.25 coincide.

#### Proof.

Once we know that both constructions give restricted Poisson structures it is enough to check that they act in the same way on the algebra generators $x_{i}$ and $y_{i}$ . We claim that in both cases $x_{i}^{[p]}=y_{i}^{[p]}=0$ . Indeed, for 3.39 this follows from $\ev_{0}(x_{i})=\ev_{0}(y_{j})=0$ . We leave this to the reader. ∎

#### Lemma 3.42.

Let $R$ be an $h$ -separable $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra. If $\phi$ is an $R$ -linear algebra automorphism of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ , then the reduction of $\phi$ modulo $h$ preserves the restricted Poisson structure on $A_{0}(R/h)$ . In other words, $\phi_{0}\in G_{0}(R/h)$ .

#### Proof.

By Remark 3.38

$$ h\cdot\{\phi_{0}(f),\phi_{0}(g)\}=[\phi(\tilde{f}),\phi(\tilde{g})]=\phi([\tilde{f},\tilde{g}])=h\cdot\phi_{0}(\{f,g\})\pmod{h^{2}} $$

thus $\phi_{0}$ preserves Poisson structure. Similarly,

$$ h^{p-1}\cdot(\phi_{0}(f))^{[p]}=(\widetilde{\phi_{0}(f)})^{p}-\mathsf{s}(\ev_{0}({\phi_{0}(f)})^{p})=\phi(\tilde{f}^{p}-\mathsf{s}(\ev_{0}({f})^{p})=h^{p-1}\cdot\phi_{0}(f^{[p]})\pmod{h^{p}}, $$

so $\phi_{0}$ also preserves the restricted structure. ∎

#### Corollary 3.43.

The map $i_{0}^{*}\colon{\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})\rightarrow i_{0*}{\underline{\Aut}}(A_{0})$ of sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ factors through $i_{0*}G_{0}$ .

Indeed, by Remark 3.37 it is enough to check on the subcategories $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ and $(\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}})^{\mathrm{op}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ . Let $\mathsf{r}\colon{\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})\rightarrow i_{0*}G_{0}$ denote the resulting map of sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ . The second result of this section concerns the kernel of the reduction map $\mathsf{r}\colon{\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})\rightarrow i_{0*}G_{0}$ . Note that $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}$ acts on $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ by conjugation and that its image lands in the kernel of $\mathsf{r}$ . Once, again it is enough to see this separately either for objects over $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ or $h$ -separable $k[h]$ -algabras. The restriction of $\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ to $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ is the whole ${\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})$ , so there is nothing to prove, while for a $k[h]$ -separable algebra $R$ the action of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)^{\times}$ on $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ by conjugation is trivial modulo $h$ since $[A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R),A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)]\subset h\cdot A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ . $$ \Ad\colon{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}\rightarrow\Ker(\mathsf{r})\subset{\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}) $$

of Zariski sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ . The map of algebras $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{S}}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ induces a homomorphism $\mathbb{G}_{m}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}$ which factors through the central elements in the center $Z(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{\mathbb{}}S})^{\times}$ .

#### Proposition 3.44.

The map $\Ad\colon{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}\rightarrow{}\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ is a surjuction of Zariski sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!\!/\mathbb{S}}$ . The kernel of $\Ad(-)$ is canonically identified with ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

#### Proof.

Again, it is enough to prove the statement for the restrictions to $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ and $(\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}})^{\mathrm{op}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ .

For $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ we have $\Ker(\mathsf{r})\simeq\underline{\Aut}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}})$ and we want to show that there is a short exact sequence

$$ 0\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{m}\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}^{\times}\rightarrow\Aut(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}})\rightarrow 0. $$

However, by Remark 3.16 we can identify $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ with the matrix algebra $\Mat_{p^{n}}$ , and the sequence above turns into

$$ 0\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{m}\rightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p^{n}}\rightarrow\mathrm{PGL}_{p^{n}}\rightarrow 0, $$

which is exact in Zariski topology.

The case of $(\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}})^{\mathrm{op}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ is much more subtle. Let us first identify the kernel of $\Ad$ . By definition it consists of the invertible elements $Z({A}_{\mathbb{S}})^{\times}$ in the center. Every element $a\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ can be uniquely written as $\sum_{I,J}r_{I,J}x^{I}y^{J}$ with $r_{I,J}\in R$ (with $I=(i_{1},\ldots,i_{n})$ , $J=(j_{1},\ldots,j_{n})$ and $0\leq i_{k},j_{l}\leq p-1$ ). Since $R$ is $h$ -torsion free, from the relations defining $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ it is clear that is $r_{I,J}\neq 0$ for some non-zero $I$ or $J$ then there is $x_{i}$ , or $y_{j}$ such that one of the commutators $[a,x_{i}]$ or $[a,y_{j}]$ is non-zero. Thus $Z(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R))^{\times}\simeq R^{\times}$ and $\Ker(\Ad(-))\simeq{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

We now pass to showing that automorphisms of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ that are trivial modulo $h$ are given by conjugation, at least after a Zariski localization $R\rightarrow R^{\prime}$ . We will first prove this after inverting $h$ , then for $h$ -completion of $R$ and then will obtain the result for $R$ using Beauville-Laszlo gluing.

If $h\in R$ is invertible then $\Spec R$ lies over $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ , and we are done by the case $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ .

If $R$ is $h$ -complete, note that $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ if also $h$ -complete (since it is free nodule of finite rank over $R$ ). We will approximate $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ by $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{n}$ for all $n\geq 0$ . As a base of induction let us show that any $\phi\in\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ is equal to an inner automorphism modulo $h^{2}$ . In other words, we would like to find $x\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)^{\times}$ such that $\phi=\Ad(x)\mod h^{2}$ . Note that the map $\phi-\id\mod h^{2}\colon A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h^{2}$ factors through $h\cdot A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ and gives a well defined map $\xi_{\phi}\colon A_{0}(R/h)\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h\rightarrow hA_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h^{2}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq A_{0}(R/h)$ , which is an $R/h$ -linear differentiation2222 22 Indeed,

$$ h\cdot\xi_{\phi}(xy)=\phi(\widetilde{x}\cdot\widetilde{y})-\widetilde{x}\cdot\widetilde{y}=\phi(\widetilde{x})\cdot\phi(\widetilde{y})-\widetilde{x}\cdot\widetilde{y}=h\cdot(\xi_{\phi}(x)\cdot y+x\cdot\xi_{\phi}(y))\pmod{h^{2}}. $$

of $A_{0}(R/h)$ . For $\phi=\Ad(x)$ with $x=x_{0}\mod h$ we have

$$ h\cdot\xi_{\Ad(x)}(a)=xax^{-1}-a=[x,a]\cdot x^{-1}=h\cdot\tfrac{1}{x_{0}}\{x_{0},a\}\pmod{h^{2}}, $$

and so one sees that $\xi_{\Ad(x)}=\frac{1}{x_{0}}H_{x_{0}}$ . Thus it is enough to show that for $\phi\in\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ the corresponding vector field $\xi_{\phi}$ is log-Hamiltonian.

The idea then is to use Lemma 3.28(2), namely we need to show that $\xi_{\phi}$ satisfies the corresponding equation (3.5). Looking at the action on commutator modulo $h^{2}$ , one sees that $\xi_{\phi}$ is Poisson (namely, $L_{\xi_{\phi}}\omega=0$ ), so Lemma 3.28(2) indeed can be applied. Moreover, it is enough to check (3.5) on $f\in I_{0}(R/h)=\{f\in A_{0}(R/h)\ |\ \ev_{0}(f)=0\}$ : indeed, the constants $R/h$ and $I_{0}(R/h)$ span all $A_{0}(R/h)$ . By 3.39, for $f\in I_{0}(R/h)$ and any lift $\tilde{f}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ we have

$$ \tilde{f}^{p}=h^{p-1}\cdot f^{[p]}\pmod{h^{p}}. $$

We then have

$$ h^{p}\cdot\xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=h^{p-1}\cdot(\phi(f^{[p]}-f^{[p]})=(\tilde{f}+h\cdot\widetilde{\xi_{\phi}(f)})^{p}-\tilde{f}^{p}\pmod{h^{p+1}}. $$

Using Jacobson’s formula (2.13) the right hand side is identified with $h^{p}(\xi_{\phi}(f)^{p}+L_{1}(\tilde{f},\widetilde{\xi_{\phi}(f)}))\pmod{h^{p+1}}$ . From this, using that $L_{1}(x,y)=\ad(x)^{p-1}(y)$ (2.14) and identifying $A_{0}(R/h)\simeq h^{p}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{p+1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ , we get that

$$ \xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=\xi_{\phi}(f)^{p}+H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi_{\phi}(f)), $$

as desired.

For $n\geq 2$ one shows analogously that if $\phi\colon A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is an automorphism which is identity modulo $h^{n}$ then there exists an element $x\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ such that $\phi=\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)$ modulo $h^{n+1}$ . Namely, such $\phi$ also defines a derivation $\xi^{\prime}_{\phi}$ of $A_{0}(R/h)$ by considering the map $\phi-\id\mod h^{n+1}\colon A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{n+1}$ which factors through $A_{h}/h\simeq A_{0}$ and whose image lies in $h^{n}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{n+1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\simeq A_{0}$ . As in the case of $n=1$ , looking at the action on the commutator one sees that $\xi^{\prime}_{\phi}$ is Poisson. However, we now have

$$ h^{n}\cdot\xi_{\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)}(a)=(1+h^{n-1}x)a(1-h^{n-1}x)=h^{n}\cdot[x_{0},a]\pmod{h^{n+1}}; $$

in other words, $\xi_{\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)}=H_{x_{0}}$ . Also, given $\phi$ that is trivial modulo $h^{n}$ with $n\geq 2$

$$ h^{p+n-1}\cdot\xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=h^{p-1}\cdot(\phi(f^{[p]}-f^{[p]})=(\tilde{f}+h^{n}\cdot\widetilde{\xi_{\phi}(f)})^{p}-\tilde{f}^{p}\pmod{h^{p+n}}, $$

from which (using Jacobson’s formula again) we get

$$ \xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi_{\phi}(f)), $$

so by Lemma 3.28(1) $\xi_{\phi}$ is Hamiltonian and $\phi$ agrees with $\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)$ for some $x$ .

This way, starting with an automorphism $\phi\in\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ , we can by induction construct a sequence of elements $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},\ldots\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ such that

$$ \phi=\ldots\circ\Ad(1+h^{2}x_{3})\circ\Ad(1+hx_{2})\circ\Ad(x_{1})=\Ad(\ldots\cdot(1+h^{2}x_{3})(1+hx_{2})x_{1}), $$

where the infinite product on the right hand side is well-defined since $R$ is $h$ -complete.

Let now $R$ be an arbitrary $h$ -separable $k[h]$ -algebra. We are trying to show that the map of (Zariski) sheaves ${\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}}\rightarrow\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ is surjective. It is enough to do so on stalks, and so we can assume $R$ is local (and, in particular, that $\Pic(R)=0$ ). Since $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is a free $R$ -module of finite rank, by Beauville-Laszlo theorem [BL], an $R$ -linear automorphism of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is uniquely encoded by a pair of automorphisms $\phi_{1}\in\Aut_{R^{\wedge}_{h}}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}))$ , $\phi_{2}\in\Aut_{R[h^{-1}]}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}]))$ (where $R^{\wedge}_{h}$ is the $h$ -adic completion of $R$ ) such that their images in $\Aut_{R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]))$ agree. By the discussion above we can find elements $a_{1}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h})$ , $a_{2}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}])$ such that $\phi_{1}=\Ad(a_{1})$ and $\phi_{2}=\Ad(a_{2})$ ; moreover, if we denote by $a_{1}^{\circ}$ , $a_{2}^{\circ}$ the images of $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$ in $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])$ then we have $\Ad(a_{1}^{\circ})=\Ad(a_{2}^{\circ})$ , so $a_{1}^{\circ}=s\cdot a_{2}^{\circ}$ for some central unit $s\in(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])^{\times}$ . Now, again by Beauville-Laszlo, one has a natural embedding of the double quotient2323 23 Which corresponds to the gluing data for a line bundle on $\Spec R$ given by trivial line bundles on $\Spec R^{\wedge}_{h}$ and $\Spec R[h^{-1}]$ and the the gluing $R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]\simeq R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]$ for the restrictions to $\Spec R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]$ given by $s\in R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]$ . $(R^{\wedge}_{h})^{\times}\backslash(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])^{\times}/R[h^{-1}]^{\times}$ to $\Pic(R)$ . Since $\Pic(R)=0$ by our assumption, it means that we can decompose $s\in(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])^{\times}$ as $s_{1}^{-1}s_{2}$ with $s_{1}\in(R^{\wedge}_{h})^{\times}$ and $s_{2}\in(R[h^{-1}])^{\times}$ . Replacing $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$ by $s_{1}a_{1}$ and $s_{2}a_{2}$ we now get $a_{1}^{\circ}=a_{2}^{\circ}$ , while still $\phi_{1}=\Ad(a_{1})$ and $\phi_{1}=\Ad(a_{2})$ . Using Beauville-Laszlo one more time the data of $a_{1}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h})$ , $a_{2}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}])$ with $a_{1}^{\circ}=a_{2}^{\circ}$ gives an element $a\in^{\times}$ . Moreover, the data of $\Ad(a_{1})\in\Aut_{R^{\wedge}_{h}}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}))$ , $\Ad(a_{2})\in\Aut_{R[h^{-1}]}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}]))$ is the same as for the $\phi$ . Thus, $\phi=\Ad(a)$ and we are done.

#### Remark 3.45.

From Proposition 3.44 we get an exact sequence of sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ :

#### Corollary 3.46.

Let $T$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -scheme and let $\pi\colon T\times\mathbb{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ be the projection. ## 4. Quasi-coherent sheaves of abelian categories

### 4.1. Sheaves of categories.

For the duration of this section a category over a commutative ring $R$ means a cocomplete abelian category ${\mathcal{C}}$ together with a ring homomorphism $R\to\Center({\mathcal{C}})$ , where $\Center({\mathcal{C}})$ is the center of ${\mathcal{C}}$ , that is the ring of endomorphisms of the identity functor $\Id\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}$ . Given such ${\mathcal{C}}$ and a homomorphism $R\to R^{\prime}$ define ${\mathcal{C}}\otimes_{R}R^{\prime}$ to be the category over $R^{\prime}$ formed by pairs $(M,\alpha)$ , where $M$ is an object of ${\mathcal{C}}$ and $\alpha\colon R^{\prime}\to\End(M)$ is a homomorphism of algebras over $R$ .

Recall the notion of a quasi-coherent sheaf of (abelian) categories over an algebraic stack due Gaitsgory ([G1, §9], [G2, §1]). Let $X$ be an algebraic stack (with respect to fpqc topology) over a base scheme $S$ such that the diagonal morphism $X\to X\times_{S}X$ is affine A quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ consists of the following data.

- (i) For every affine scheme $Z$ over $X$ a category ${\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ over ${\mathcal{O}}(Z)$ .

- (ii) For every morphism $u\colon Z^{\prime}\to Z$ of affine schemes over $X$ , an equivalence

$$ u^{*}\colon{\mathfrak{S}}(Z)\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}(Z)}{\mathcal{O}}(Z^{\prime})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathfrak{S}}(Z^{\prime}), $$

of categories over ${\mathcal{O}}(Z^{\prime})$ .

- (iii) For every composable pair of morphisms $u_{1}$ , $u_{2}$ of affine schemes over $X$ , an isomorphism $(u_{1}\circ u_{2})^{*}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}u_{2}^{*}\circ u_{1}^{*}$ such that the natural compatibility axiom for $3$ -fold compositions holds.

Given a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ the category ${\mathfrak{S}}(X)$ of its global sections is defined to be $\mathop{\displaystyle\lim_{\longleftarrow}}{\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ , where the limit is taken over the category of affine schemes over $X$ . Given any morphism $u\colon Z\to X$ we shall write ${\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ for the category of global sections of the pullback of ${\mathfrak{S}}$ to $Z$ . According to [G2, Proposition 8] ${\mathfrak{S}}$ has the sheaf property: for a faithfully flat cover $u\colon Z\to X$ the category ${\mathfrak{S}}(X)$ is equivalent to the category of descent data on ${\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ . A key result proven in is the faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent sheaves of categories: for $u$ as above, giving a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $X$ is equivalent to giving a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $Z$ together with descent data.

Note that if $X=\Spec{\mathcal{O}}(X)$ is an affine scheme then giving a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ is equivalent to giving a category ${\mathfrak{S}}(S)$ over ${\mathcal{O}}(S)$ .

#### Example 4.1.

Let $A$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -algebras. For a morphism $u\colon Z\to X$ , define a category $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)$ to be the category of quasi-coherent sheaves of $u^{*}A$ -modules on $Z$ . This construction determines a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $X$ denoted by $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . In particular, ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $X$ with ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\QCoh(Z)$ , for any stack $Z$ mapping to $X$ .

### 4.2. Groups acting on a category.

For an affine group scheme $H$ over $S$ acting on $X$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ an $H$ -equivariant structure on ${\mathfrak{S}}$ consists of a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}_{X/H}$ over the quotient stack $X/H$ together with an equivalence of quasi-coherent sheaves of categories between the pullback of ${\mathfrak{S}}_{X/H}$ to $X$ and ${\mathfrak{S}}$ . In particular, if $H$ acts trivially on $X$ we shall refer to the above data as an action of $H$ on ${\mathfrak{S}}$ .

The following construction will play an important role in what follows.

## 5. Action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ .

### 5.1. Main Theorem.

The action of $G_{0}$ on $A_{0}$ defines its action on $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . The goal of this subsection is to extend the latter to an action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ .

#### Theorem 1.

Let $H$ be an affine group scheme over ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ equipped with a homomorphism $\upsilon\colon H\to G_{0}$ . There exists a unique (up to a unique isomorphism) action of the group scheme $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ equipped with a trivialization at $h=\infty$ such that the induced action of $H$ on the center of $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ (identified with $A_{0}$ ) equals the composition $H\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\upsilon}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{0}\hookrightarrow\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ .

#### Remark 5.1.

Set $H_{\mathbb{S}}=H\times\mathbb{S}$ . We claim that giving an action of $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ amounts specifying an extension

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{S}}}),} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ad} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha} $$

satisfying property (T) in Construction 4.2. Indeed, using Remark 4.4 it suffices to check that, for any affine scheme $Z$ over $\mathbb{S}$ , every autoequivalence $\phi$ of the category ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z){\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ over ${\mathcal{O}}(Z)$ fpqc locally on $Z$ preserves the isomorphism class of the free ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ -module ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ . We shall see that this is true even Zariski locally on $Z$ . We may assume that ${\mathcal{O}}(Z)$ is a local ring. If the image of $Z$ in $\mathbb{S}$ does not contain $0$ then ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ is an Azumaya algebra. Hence, $\phi$ is given by the tensor product with a line bundle over $Z$ . Since $Z$ is local $\phi$ is isomorphic to the identity functor. If $Z\to\mathbb{S}$ maps the closed point to $0$ then ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ is a local ring. Hence, by Kaplansky’s theorem, every projective ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ -module is free. In particular, this can be applied to a projective module $\phi({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z))$ . Using that the ring of endomorphisms of $\phi({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z))$ is a local ring (namely, ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)^{op}$ ) we conclude that $\phi({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z))$ is indecomposable. This proves the claim. We remark that the argument above also shows that $\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}$ viewed as a $\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}$ -torsor over $H_{\mathbb{S}}$ is locally trivial for the Zariski topology on $H_{\mathbb{S}}$ .

Under this equivalence a trivialization of the action at $h=\infty$ amounts to the choice of a section $H=H\times\infty\to\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\infty$ whose image commutes with the subgroup $\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\infty\subset\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\infty$ . $$ \widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}0\to H_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}0\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\upsilon}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{0}\subset\underline{\Aut}(A_{0}), $$

together with chosen sections at $h=\infty$ , there exists a unique isomorphism connecting the two that carries one section to the other.

We start with the uniqueness assertion. Let $T$ be an affine scheme over ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ , $\pi\colon T\times{\mathbb{S}}\to\mathbb{S}$ the projection. The tensor product with a line bundle defines a functor

$$ \Pic(T\times\mathbb{S})\to\Aut(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}) $$

#### Lemma 5.2.

Functor (5.2) is fully faithful and its essential image consists of those autoequivalences ${\mathfrak{H}}\subset\Aut(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})$ that act identically on the center of $(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})_{|T\times 0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ (identified with $A_{0}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}(T)$ ).

The only part that requires a proof is the essential surjectivity of the functor $\Pic(T\times\mathbb{S})\to{\mathfrak{H}}$ . Let $\phi$ be an autoequivalence in ${\mathfrak{H}}$ . We claim that $\phi$ , locally for the Zariski topology on $T\times\mathbb{S}$ , is isomorphic to $\Id$ . Indeed, as explained in Remark 5.1, every autoequivalence of $\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is, locally on $T\times\mathbb{S}$ , induced by an automorphism of $\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . Since $\phi\in{\mathfrak{H}}$ the latter automorphism is equal to $\Id$ modulo $h$ . Now the claim follows from Lemma 3.46. Assigning to every open subset $U\subset T\times\mathbb{S}$ the set of isomorphisms $\phi_{|U}\simeq\Id$ we define a torsor (for the Zariski topology) under the sheaf of central elements in $(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})^{*}$ . The latter sheaf is equal to ${\mathcal{O}}^{*}_{\mathbb{S}\times T}$ . This defines a line bundle $L_{\phi}$ over $T\times\mathbb{S}$ such that $\phi$ is the tensor product with $L_{\phi}$ . ∎

Next, consider the groupoid ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ formed by pairs $(\phi,\alpha)$ , where $\phi\in{\mathfrak{H}}$ and $\alpha\colon\phi_{|T\times\infty}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Id$ . The equivalence $\Pic(T\times\mathbb{S})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathfrak{H}}$ induces an equivalence between ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ and the groupoid of line bundles over $T\times\mathbb{S}$ equipped with a trivialization at $T\times\infty$ . Since the Picard stack of $\mathbb{S}={\mathbb{P}}^{1}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$ is isomorphic to ${\mathbb{Z}}\times B{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ it follows that ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ is discrete and its $\pi_{0}$ is the group $H^{0}(T,{\mathbb{Z}})$ .

Returning to the proof of the uniqueness assertion recall that giving an action $\psi$ of $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is equivalent to giving descent data along the morphism $\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}\times BH$ . In particular, any action gives rise to an autoequivalence

$$ \phi\colon\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}, $$

where $\pi\colon H\times\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is the projection. If $\phi_{1}$ , $\phi_{2}$ are equipped with trivializations at $h=\infty$ and induce the same action on the center of $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ then $\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}^{-1}$ is an object of ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ corresponding to some element $[\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}^{-1}]\in H^{0}(H,{\mathbb{Z}})$ . Using the cocycle isomorphisms related to $\phi_{i}$ it follows that $[\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}^{-1}]$ is, in fact, a group homomorphism $H\to{\mathbb{Z}}$ . The latter must be trivial because $H$ is assumed to be affine and, in particular, quasi-compact. We conclude that there is a unique isomorphism $\phi_{1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\phi_{2}$ that commutes with trivializations at $H\times\infty$ . The discreteness of ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ (applied to $T=H\times H$ ) implies that $\phi_{1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\phi_{2}$ commutes with cocycle isomorphisms. This completes the proof of the uniqueness assertion of the Theorem.
